Hence Cov(Y,D|X)=Var(D|X) h(X)>0 for every X. Partialling out X, with rD=D-proj_{1,X}D and rY=Y-proj_{1,X}Y,
β3 = Cov(rD,rY)/Var(rD). Because D ⟂ Y0,Y1|X,
E[rD Y|X]=Var(D|X) h(X)>0,
so in expectation
β3 = E[ Var(D|X) h(X) ] / E[ Var(D|X) ]  up to the positive weight coming from the linear projection of D on X.
It is a positive weighted average of the strictly positive conditional effects h(X)=E[τ|X]. In particular E[Y|D=1,X]-E[Y|D=0,X]=h(X)>0 for every X, so the conditional mean is monotone increasing in D holding X fixed and the best linear approximation of that monotone conditional mean in the space {1,D,X} must load D with a positive sign.

Once X is in the regression the X-induced selection that can flip the sign in Case 2 is removed. The sign is therefore guaranteed in the unconditionally randomised regression and in the X-adjusted regression under conditional randomisation, but not in the uncontrolled marginal regression under conditional randomisation.
public_text.11:
The population linear projection is not the conditional mean.  

Write $Y_{0}=m(X)$ $m(x)=E[Y_{0}\mid X=x]$, $h(x)=E[Y_{1}-Y_{0}\mid X=x]>0$ and 
$p(x)=P(D=1\mid X=x)$.  Unconfoundedness is  

$E[Y\mid X,D]=m(X)+D\,h(X), \qquad h>0\;a.s.$

Case 1 $D\perp (Y_{0},Y_{1})$. Then
$\beta_{1}=E[Y\mid D=1]-E[Y\mid D=0]=E[Y_{1}]-E[Y_{0}]=E[\tau]>0$,
the usual ATE.

Case 2 $D\perp (Y_{0},Y_{1})\mid X$ but $X$ is omitted.  

$$
E[Y\mid D=1]-E[Y\mid D=0]
=E[h(X)\mid D=1]+E[m(X)\mid D=1]-E[m(X)\mid D=0].
$$

The first term is $>0$ but $E[m(X)\mid D=1]-E[m(X)\mid D=0]$ is the
selection bias $Cov(p(X),m(X))/\!Var(D)$ and is unrestricted under
conditional randomisation.  With $p(x)$ decreasing in $m(x)$ the bias can
dominate $E[h\mid D=1]$.  E.g. $X\in\{0,1\}$, $p(0)=1,p(1)=0$, $m(x)=x$,
$h\equiv0.1$, gives $E[Y\mid D=1]-E[Y\mid D=0]=0.1-1<0$ although
$Y_{1}>Y_{0}$ a.s.

Case 3 the Frisch-Waugh coefficient on $D$ after linear control for $X$ is

$$
\beta_{D}=\frac{Cov\!\big(D\,,\,Y\big)}{Var(D)} \;\text{on the space }
\{1,X\}.
$$

Let $\tilde D=D-\operatorname{proj}_{1,X}D$, $v(x)=p(x)-\operatorname{proj}_{1,X}p(x)$,
$E[v]=E[vX]=0$. Then

$$
Cov(\tilde D,Y)=E\big[v(X)m(X)\big]+E\big[p(X)v(X)h(X)\big]
               =E\!\left[v(X)E[Y\mid X]\right].
$$

$E[D\tilde D\mid X]=p(x)v(x)$ so $E[pv h]>0$, but $E[v m]$ is free.
With a non-linear $m(\cdot)$ and a non-linear $p(\cdot)$ the linear
residual $v(X)$ can be made negatively correlated with $m(X)+p(X)h(X)$.
E.g. $X=-1,0,1$ equiprob., $p(-1)=p(1)=0.9,\;p(0)=0.1$, $h\equiv1$,
$m(x)=-k x^{2}$.  Then $\operatorname{proj}_{1,X}p$ is constant,
$v(-1)=v(1)>0,\;v(0)<0$ and

$Cov(\tilde D,Y)=E[v m]+E[pv]\propto -k\,E[vX^{2}]+{\rm const}<0$

for $k$ large enough, while $h(x)>0$ a.s. and $D\perp(Y_{0},Y_{1})\mid X$.
The linear control absorbs only the linear part of $m$ and $p$; the
non-linear remainder can be used by $D$ to proxy $m(X)$ and reverse the
sign.  The same Simpson reversal occurs with $m(x)=x^{2}$.

Hence positivity of the individual effect $\tau_{i}>0$ a.s. guarantees
positivity of the unconditional randomised mean difference, but it does
not guarantee positivity of the marginal mean difference under
conditional randomisation nor of the linear projection on $1,D,X$.
The only sign guaranteed case is the unconditionally randomised one.

A. Only Case 1
public_text.12:
The population OLS coefficient is the linear projection coefficient.

Write $Y=Y_{0}+D\tau$, $\tau_{i}>0$ a.s., $m_{0}(X)=E[Y_{0}|X]$,
$\tau(X)=E[\tau|X]>0$ and $p(X)=E[D|X]$ so that under conditional
randomisation

$E[Y|X,D]=m_{0}(X)+D\,\tau(X)$,  $D\perp(Y_{0},\tau)|X$.

Case 1.  $D\perp(Y_{0},Y_{1})$.
$$
\beta_{1}=E[Y|D=1]-E[Y|D=0]=E[Y_{1}]-E[Y_{0}]=E[\tau]>0,
$$
the difference in means, i.e. the ATE, is strictly positive.

Case 2.  $D\perp(Y_{0},Y_{1})|X$ but $p(X)$ may depend on $X$.
$$
E[Y|D=1]-E[Y|D=0]=E[\tau(X)|D=1]+E[m_{0}(X)|D=1]-E[m_{0}(X)|D=0].
$$
The first term is $>0$ but $E[m_{0}(X)|D=1]-E[m_{0}(X)|D=0]$ is unrestricted
by unconfoundedness.  With $p(X)$ decreasing in $m_{0}(X)$ the selection
bias can dominate the positive treatment term, e.g. $X\in\{0,1\}$,
$p(0)=1$, $p(1)=0$, $m_{0}(0)=0$, $m_{0}(1)=100$, $\tau\equiv0.1$ gives
$E[Y|D=1]=0.1<1=E[Y|D=0]$ although $\tau_{i}>0$ a.s.  The marginal
difference in means is not signed.

Case 3.  Let $\hat p(X)= \operatorname{proj}_{1,X}p(X)=a+bX$ and
$D_{r}=D-\hat p(X)$.  Then
$$
E[D_{r}Y]=E\big[(p(X)-\hat p(X))\,E[Y|X]\big]
       =E\big[(p-\hat p)\big(m_{0}+ \tau p\big)\big]
       =E\big[(p-\hat p)m_{0}\big]+E\big[\tau p(1-\hat p)\big]+E\big[(p-\hat p)p\tau\big].
$$
$E[D_{r}Y|X]=E[\tau(X)\operatorname{Var}(D|X)]>0$ pointwise, so
${\rm Cov}(Y,D|X)>0$, but the linear projection removes only the linear
part of $p(X)$ and $m_{0}(X)$.  The term $E[(p-\hat p)m_{0}(X)]$ is the
covariance of the non-linear part of $p(X)$ with the non-linear part of
$m_{0}(X)$ and can be made arbitrarily negative.

E.g. $X=1,2,3$ equiprobable, $p(1)=0.1,p(2)=0.9,p(3)=0.5$,
$m_{0}(X)=X^{2}$, $\tau\equiv0.1>0$.
$\hat p(X)=0.1+0.2X$, $p-\hat p=-0.2,0.4,-0.2$ and
$$
E[(p-\hat p)E[Y|X]]=\tfrac13\big[-0.2(1.01)+0.4(4.09)-0.2(9.05)\big]<0,
$$
so
$$
\beta_{3}= \frac{E[D_{r}Y]}{E[D_{r}^{2}]}<0
$$
in the population regression $Y=\alpha+\beta_{D}D+\gamma X+u$ while
$E[Y|D=1,X]-E[Y|D=0,X]=\tau(X)>0$ for every $X$ and $\tau_{i}>0$ a.s.
The linear $X$ control soaks up only the linear component of $m_{0}$ and
$p$; the remaining non-linear remainder can be used by $D$ as a proxy for
$m_{0}$ and reverse the sign.

Hence a strictly positive population OLS slope on $D$ is guaranteed only
under unconditional randomisation. Cases 2 and the linearly controlled
Case 3 can both be sign reversed by selection on $X$ and by linear
misspecification of $m_{0}(X)$.

A. Only Case 1
public_text.4:
The OLS coefficient is the linear projection of $Y$ on the regressors.
Write $Y=Y_{0}+D\tau$, $\tau>0$ a.s., $m(X)=E[Y_{0}|X]$, $h(X)=E[\tau|X]>0$
and $p(X)=E[D|X]$.  Under $D\perp (Y_{0},\tau)|X$

$$
E[Y|X,D]=m(X)+D\,h(X),\qquad 
{\rm Cov}(Y,D|X)=h(X){\rm Var}(D|X)>0 .
$$

Case 1. $D\perp(Y_{0},Y_{1})$.
$$
\beta_{1}= \frac{{\rm Cov}(D,Y)}{{\rm Var}(D)}
        =E[Y|D=1]-E[Y|D=0]=E[Y_{1}]-E[Y_{0}]=E[\tau]>0 .
$$
Unconditional randomisation is the ATE and is strictly positive.

Case 2. $D\perp(Y_{0},Y_{1})|X$ but $D$ may be correlated with $X$.
$$
E[Y|D=1]-E[Y|D=0]
 =E[h(X)|D=1]+E[m(X)|D=1]-E[m(X)|D=0].
$$
The first term is $>0$ but the selection term $E[m(X)|D=1]-E[m(X)|D=0]$
is unrestricted by conditional randomisation.  With $p(X)$ decreasing in
$m(X)$ the bias can dominate the positive treatment term, e.g.
$X\in\{0,1\},p(0)=1,p(1)=0,m(0)=0,m(1)=100,\tau\equiv0.1$ gives
$E[Y|D=1]-E[Y|D=0]<0$ although $\tau>0$ a.s.  The marginal difference in
means is not signed.

Case 3.  The population linear projection $Y=a+bD+cX+u$ is
$b={\rm Cov}(D_{\rm res},Y)/{\rm Var}(D_{\rm res})$ with
$D_{\rm res}=D-{\rm proj}_{1,X}D$.
$$
{\rm Cov}(D_{\rm res},Y)
 ={\rm Cov}\!\big(D_{\rm res},m(X)\big)+E\!\big[D_{\rm res}D\,h(X)\big].
$$
The second term is positive but
${\rm Cov}(D_{\rm res},m(X))={\rm Cov}(p(X)-{\rm proj}_{1,X}p(X),\,m(X))$
is the covariance of the non-linear part of $p(X)$ with the possibly
non-linear baseline $m(X)$.  It is unrestricted by
$D\perp(Y_{0},Y_{1})|X$ and can be made arbitrarily negative.

E.g. $X\in\{-1,0,1\}$ equiprobable,
$p(-1)=p(1)=0.9,\;p(0)=0.1$, $m(-1)=m(1)=0,\;m(0)=300$, $h\equiv1$.
Then $E[XY]=E[XD]=0$, so $c=0$ and
$$
b=\frac{E[DY]-E[D]E[Y]}{{\rm Var}(D)}<0,
$$
while $E[Y|D,X]=m(X)+D$ is strictly increasing in $D$ for every $X$.
Hence the linear $X$ control does not preserve the pointwise monotonicity
$E[Y|D,X]$ and the linear projection coefficient can change sign.  In
particular $Cov(Y,D|X)>0$ for every $X$ does not imply $Cov(Y,D_{\rm res})>0$.

Positivity of the population OLS slope is therefore guaranteed only
under unconditional randomisation, i.e. Case 1.  Cases 2 and 3 can be
reversed by selection on $X$ and by the linear misspecification of
$m(X)$.

A. Only Case 1

4.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The individual effect is $\tau_i=Y_{1i}-Y_{0i}>0$ a.s. and under
$D\perp(Y_{0},Y_{1})|X$

$E[Y|X,D]=m_{0}(X)+D\,h(X)$ with $m_{0}(X)=E[Y_{0}|X]$ and $h(X)=E[\tau|X]>0$ a.s.,
$p(X)=E[D|X]$, ${\rm Cov}(Y,D|X)=h(X){\rm Var}(D|X)>0$.

Case 1 $D\perp(Y_{0},Y_{1})$. Then
$\beta_{1}=E[Y|D=1]-E[Y|D=0]=E[Y_{1}]-E[Y_{0}]=E[\tau]>0$, the OLS slope is the ATE. Sign guaranteed.

Case 2 $D\perp(Y_{0},Y_{1})|X$ but $D$ is allowed to depend on $X$ and $X$ is omitted.
$E[Y|D=1]-E[Y|D=0]=E[h(X)|D=1]+E[m_{0}(X)|D=1]-E[m_{0}(X)|D=0]$.
The selection term $E[m_{0}|D=1]-E[m_{0}|D=0]$ is unrestricted by conditional randomisation.
With $p(X)$ decreasing in $m_{0}(X)$ the bias can dominate the positive $E[h|D=1]$ term.
E.g. $X\in\{0,1\}$, $p(0)=1,p(1)=0$, $m_{0}(0)=0,m_{0}(1)=100$, $\tau\equiv0.1$ gives $E[Y|D=1]<E[Y|D=0]$.
Hence the marginal difference in means, i.e. the $1,D$ OLS, is not signed.

Case 3 $1,D,X$ linear projection. Let $\tilde D=D-{\rm proj}_{1,X}D$, $v(X)=p(X)-{\rm proj}_{1,X}p(X)$.
Frisch–Waugh gives
${\rm Cov}(\tilde D,Y)=E[h(X){\rm Var}(D|X)]+{\rm Cov}\big(v(X),m_{0}(X)+p(X)h(X)\big)$.
The first term $E[h\,{\rm Var}(D|X)]>0$ is the non-parametric partial covariance.
The second term is the covariance of the linear-approximation error of $p(X)$ with the possibly non-linear baseline $m_{0}(X)+p(X)h(X)$. It is unrestricted by unconfoundedness and $h>0$.
With a non-linear $m_{0}$ and non-linear $p$ the term ${\rm Cov}(v,m_{0})$ can be made arbitrarily negative and dominate the positive $E[h\,{\rm Var}(D|X)]$ term.
Classic examples: $X\in\{-1,0,1\}$ equiprobable, $p(-1)=p(1)=0.9,p(0)=0.1$, $m_{0}(-1)=m_{0}(1)=0,m_{0}(0)=300$, $h\equiv1$ gives $E[Y|D,X]=m_{0}(X)+D$ strictly increasing in $D$ for every $X$ yet ${\rm Cov}(\tilde D,Y)<0$, so the linear coefficient on $D$ in $Y\sim1+D+X$ is negative. Similarly $X\sim U[-1,1]$, $p(x)=0.5+0.4x^{2}$, $m_{0}(x)=-k x^{2}$, $h\equiv0.1$ gives $\beta_{3}\propto-0.0356k+0.023<0$ for $k\gtrsim1$.

Hence $Cov(Y,D|X)>0$ pointwise does not imply $Cov(Y_{\perp X},D_{\perp X})>0$ for the linear residual $D_{\perp X}=D-{\rm proj}_{1,X}D$. The non-parametric partial effect $E[Var(D|X)h(X)]/E[Var(D|X)]>0$ is positive, but the linear projection can suffer sign reversal because the linear span $\{1,X\}$ does not span $m_{0}(X)$ and $p(X)$ in general; the residual $v(X)$ can proxy the non-linear part of $m_{0}$.

The colleagues arguing for E – Only Case 1 and Case 3 – conflate the non-parametric partial covariance with the linear projection coefficient. While $E[Y|D=1,X]-E[Y|D=0,X]=h(X)>0$ for every $X$ holds, the best linear approximation to $m_{0}(X)+D h(X)$ in the space $\{1,D,X\}$ need not be monotone in $D$ when $m_{0}$ and $p$ are non-linear. The sign guarantee survives the unconditional randomised case, and would survive a fully non-parametric control for $X$, but it does not survive a linear control for $X$.

Thus the only case where positivity of $\tau_i>0$ a.s. forces a positive population OLS coefficient on $D$ is unconditional randomisation. Cases 2 and 3 can both be sign-reversed by $X$-dependent propensity and non-linear $m_{0}$. Current best belief: A. Only Case 1.

12.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The individual effect is τ_i=Y1i−Y0i>0 a.s. and under conditional randomisation
E[Y|X,D]=m0(X)+D τ(X) with τ(X)=E[τ|X]>0, p(X)=E[D|X].

Case 1: D⊥(Y0,Y1). Then β1 =E[Y|D=1]−E[Y|D=0]=E[Y1]−E[Y0]=E[τ]>0.
Unconditional randomisation gives the ATE and the ordinary difference in means is strictly positive.

Case 2: D⊥(Y0,Y1)|X but D may depend on X.
E[Y|D=1]−E[Y|D=0]=E[τ(X)|D=1]+E[m0(X)|D=1]−E[m0(X)|D=0].
The first term >0 but the selection term E[m0(X)|D=1]−E[m0(X)|D=0] is unrestricted by unconfoundedness. With p(X) decreasing in m0(X) the bias can dominate the positive treatment term, e.g. X∈{0,1}, p0=1,p1=0, m0(0)=0,m0(1)=100, τ≡0.1 gives E[Y|D=1]=0.1<1=E[Y|D=0]. The marginal OLS coefficient need not be positive.

Case 3: Linear projection of Y on 1,D,X. Let proj_{1,X}D=α+βX and r(X)=p(X)−α−βX. Then
E[(D−α−βX)Y]=E[r(X)(m0(X)+τ(X)p(X))].
Cov(Y,D|X)=Var(D|X)τ(X)>0, but the linear residual r(X) is orthogonal only to 1,X, not to m0(X). Because m0(·) and p(·) can be non-linear the term E[r(X)m0(X)] can be made arbitrarily negative relative to the positive E[r(X)τ(X)p(X)].

A concrete discrete example shows reversal: X=1,2,3 equiprobable, p(1)=0.1,p(2)=0.9,p(3)=0.5, m0(X)=X², τ≡0.1>0. Then proj_{1,X}p=0.1+0.2X, r=−0.2,0.4,−0.2 and E[r(m0+τp)]<0, so the population Frisch-Waugh coefficient on D is negative while τ>0 a.s. and D⊥(Y0,Y1)|X. The linear X control soaks up only the linear part of m0 and p; the non-linear remainder can be used by D as a proxy for m0 and flip the sign. Same Simpson-type reversal with X∼U[-1,1], p(x)=0.5+0.4x², m0(x)=−k x² gives β∝−0.0356k+0.023<0 for k large.

Hence a strictly positive population OLS slope is guaranteed only under unconditional randomisation. Case 2 and the linearly controlled Case 3 can both be signed the wrong way by selection on X and by linear misspecification of m0(X). The E camp that claims Case 3 must be positive conflates the non-parametric partial covariance E[Var(D|X)τ(X)]>0 with the linear projection Cov(Y,D⊥X)>0. With only a linear term in X the projection residual D−proj_{1,X}D is not mean independent of m0(X), so positivity of the conditional mean in D does not imply positivity of the linear coefficient.

The split in the room between E Only Case1 and Case3 and A Only Case1 reflects the common confusion between conditional mean positivity Cov(Y,D|X)>0 and positivity of the linear projection coefficient when m0(X) is non-linear. The correct non-parametric conclusion with no parametric restriction on m0 is A.

Current belief remains A. Only Case 1 must be positive.

10.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The core model is Y = Y0 + D τ, τ>0 a.s., D ⟂ (Y0,τ) | X, so E[Y|X,D]=m0(X)+D h(X) with h(X)=E[τ|X]>0 a.s., p(X)=E[D|X]. 

Case 1 unconditional randomisation: β1 = E[Y|D=1]-E[Y|D=0]=E[τ]>0. Uncontroversial.

Case 2 marginal regression under conditional randomisation: 
E[Y|D=1]-E[Y|D=0]=E[h(X)|D=1]+E[m0(X)|D=1]-E[m0(X)|D=0].
The selection term E[m0|X]|D=1 - E[m0|X]|D=0 is unrestricted by D ⟂ (Y0,τ)|X. With p(X) decreasing in m0(X) the marginal difference in means can be made arbitrarily negative while τ>0 a.s., e.g. Y0=X, τ≡0.1, p(x)=1{x<0}. So the uncontrolled OLS slope is not sign identified.

Case 3 Y on 1,D,X is the linear projection. Let D̃ = D - proj_{1,X}D and r(X)=E[D̃|X]=p(X)-proj_{1,X}p(X). Then
Cov(Y,D̃)=E[Cov(Y,D|X)]+Cov(E[Y|X],r(X))
       =E[Var(D|X)h(X)]+Cov(m0(X)+p(X)h(X), r(X)).
The first term >0. The second term is the covariance of the linear-approximation error of p(X) with the linear-approximation error of m0(X)+p(X)h(X). Unconfoundedness does not restrict it. With a non-linear m0(·) and non-linear p(·) the term Cov(r(X),m0(X)) can be made arbitrarily negative and dominate E[Var(D|X)h(X)].

Explicit sign reversal: X∈{-1,0,1} equiprobable, m0(x)=x², h≡0.1, p(-1)=0.1,p(0)=0.9,p(1)=0.5. Then E[Y|X,D]=x²+0.1D is strictly increasing in D for every X, yet proj_{1,X}D is linear in X and Cov(D̃,Y)<0, giving Frisch-Waugh coefficient ≈-0.5<0 while τ>0 a.s. and D ⟂ (Y0,Y1)|X. Same construction works with continuous X, e.g. p(x)=0.5+0.4x², m0(x)=-k x², h≡0.1 giving β3∝-0.0356k+0.023<0 for k large.

Thus Cov(Y,D|X)>0 pointwise does not imply Cov(Y⊥X,D⊥X)>0 for the linear residuals. The non-parametric residual D-E[D|X] is guaranteed positive, but the linear residual D-proj_{1,X}D is not.

The E camp argues β3 = E[Var(D|X)h(X)]/E[Var(D|X)]>0 by partialling out X, i.e. using D-E[D|X] rather than D-proj_{1,X}D, and assumes the linear control removes the selection channel. That holds if m0(X) and p(X) are linear in X, but no such parametric restriction is given.

Hence positivity of the individual effect forces positivity only under unconditional randomisation. Under conditional randomisation the marginal slope Case 2 can be negative, and the linearly controlled slope Case 3 can also be negative by linear misspecification of m0(X) and p(X). Current belief remains A. Only Case 1.

3.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The population OLS coefficient is the linear projection of Y on the regressors.

Write Y = Y0 + D τ with τ>0 a.s. and under conditional randomisation
E[Y|X,D]= m0(X)+ D h(X) with m0(X)=E[Y0|X], h(X)=E[τ|X]>0,
p(X)=E[D|X], D⊥(Y0,τ)|X.

Case 1 D⊥(Y0,Y1). β1 = E[Y|D=1]-E[Y|D=0]=E[Y1]-E[Y0]=E[τ]>0.
Unconditional randomisation identifies the ATE and sign is guaranteed.

Case 2 D⊥(Y0,Y1)|X but regression is Y~1+D.
E[Y|D=1]-E[Y|D=0]=E[h(X)|D=1]+E[m0(X)|D=1]-E[m0(X)|D=0].
The selection term E[m0|D=1]-E[m0|D=0]=Cov(p,m0)/Var(D) is unrestricted.
With p(X) decreasing in m0(X) the bias can dominate E[h|D=1].
E.g. X∈{0,1}, p0=1,p1=0,m0(0)=0,m0(1)=100,τ≡0.1 gives
E[Y|D=1]=0.1<1=E[Y|D=0] although τ>0 a.s. Sign not guaranteed.

Case 3 Y~1+D+X linear projection.
Let D̃ = D - proj_{1,X} D, v(X)=p(X)-proj_{1,X}p(X), E[v]=E[vX]=0.
E[Y D̃|X]= v(X)[m0(X)+p(X)h(X)] + h(X)p(X)(1-p(X)).
Hence
Cov(Y,D̃)=E[h(X)p(X)(1-p(X))]+E[v(X)(m0(X)+p(X)h(X))].
First term >0. Second term =Cov(v, E[Y|X]) is unrestricted by unconfoundedness.
With m0 non-linear in X the linear space {1,X} does not span m0 and v can be made
negatively correlated with m0 + p h to dominate the positive first term.
E.g. X=1,2,3 equiprobable, m0(X)=X², h≡0.1, p(1)=0.1,p(2)=0.9,p(3)=0.5 gives
proj_{1,X}D linear in X and Cov(D̃,Y)<0 while E[Y|D=1,X]-E[Y|D=0,X]=h>0 a.s.
Same Simpson reversal with p(x)=0.5+0.4x², m0(x)=-k x².

Thus Cov(Y,D|X)=Var(D|X)h(X)>0 pointwise, so the non-parametric
partial effect is positive, but the linear projection onto {1,D,X} is not.
The E camp confuses the non-parametric residual D-E[D|X] with the linear
residual D-proj_{1,X}D and assumes Cov(D̃,m0)=0. Under conditional
randomisation Cov(D,m0|X)=0, but Cov(D̃,m0)≠0 when m0 is non-linear.

Positivity of τ_i>0 guarantees positivity of the unadjusted slope only
under unconditional randomisation. With conditional randomisation the
marginal slope in Case 2 and the linearly adjusted slope in Case 3 can both
be signed the wrong way by selection on X and by linear misspecification
of E[Y0|X]. Consensus in the deliberation is split, with a minority claiming
Case 3 is guaranteed by E[Y|D=1,X]-E[Y|D=0,X]>0. That claim holds for the
non-parametric partial regression, not for the population linear projection
Y~1+D+X with unrestricted m0.

Current belief: sign is guaranteed only in Case 1. Option A. Only Case 1 and Case 3 remain disputed; the error is the linear vs non-parametric residual distinction.

11.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The core structure is Y = Y0 + D τ, τ_i>0 a.s., E[Y|X,D]=m0(X)+D h(X) with h(X)=E[τ|X]>0 a.s., D⊥(Y0,τ)|X, p(X)=E[D|X], m0(X)=E[Y0|X].

Case 1 D⊥(Y0,Y1). β1 = E[Y|D=1]-E[Y|D=0]=E[Y1]-E[Y0]=E[τ]>0. Uncontroversial.

Case 2 D⊥(Y0,Y1)|X but X omitted. 
E[Y|D=1]-E[Y|D=0]=E[h(X)|D=1]+E[m0(X)|D=1]-E[m0(X)|D=0].
The selection term E[m0|X]|D=1 - E[m0|X]|D=0 = Cov(p,m0)/Var(D) is unrestricted. With p(x) decreasing in m0(x) e.g. jobs program targeted at low pre-income, the bias can dominate the positive E[h|D=1] term. Discrete example X∈{0,1}, p0=1,p1=0, m0(0)=0,m0(1)=100, τ≡0.1 gives negative marginal difference despite τ>0 a.s. So marginal constant-D regression is not sign guaranteed.

Case 3 Y regressed on 1,D,X linearly. Frisch-Waugh β_D = Cov(Y,D̃)/Var(D̃) with D̃ = D - proj_{1,X}D. 
E[D̃|X]=p(X)-a-bX ≠0 unless p linear. 
E[D̃ Y|X]=E[D̃|X]E[Y|X]+Var(D|X)h(X).
Hence E[D̃ Y]=E[E[D̃|X]E[Y|X]]+E[Var(D|X)h(X)].
Second term >0. First term = E[(p-proj p)(m0+ph)] can be made arbitrarily negative by non-linear p and m0.
Indeed with E[D̃|X]=p-a-bX, 
E[D̃Y|X]=E[D̃|X](m0+ p h)+p(1-p)h.
The term E[D̃|X](m0+ph) is unrestricted by unconfoundedness. 
Explicit three-point example X=1,2,3 equiprobable, m0(x)=x², h≡0.1, p(1)=0.1,p(2)=0.9,p(3)=0.5 gives proj p linear, Cov(D̃,Y)<0 while h>0 a.s. and E[Y|D=1,X]-E[Y|D=0,X]=h>0 for every X. 
The same reversal occurs with p(x)=0.5+0.4x², m0(x)=-k x², h≡0.1 giving β∝ -0.0356k+0.023, negative for k large.

Thus Cov(Y,D|X)>0 pointwise does not imply Cov(Y,D̃)>0 for linear residual. The E camp argues E[D̃ Y|X]=Var(D|X)h>0, which uses the non-parametric residual D-E[D|X] where E[D̃|X]=0. With linear projection E[D̃|X]≠0, the extra term E[E[D̃|X]E[Y|X]] can flip sign.

So positivity of individual effect guarantees positivity of unconditional randomised mean difference, but not of the marginal mean difference under conditional randomisation, nor of the linearly controlled projection. The only guaranteed case is Case 1.

Current belief: A. Only Case 1. Cases 2 and 3 can be sign reversed by selection on X and by linear misspecification of m0 and p.

8.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The model is $Y=Y_{0}+D\tau$, $\tau_i>0$ a.s., $E[Y|X,D]=m_0(X)+D\,h(X)$ with $h(X)=E[\tau|X]>0$ a.s. and $D\perp(Y_0,\tau)|X$, $p(X)=E[D|X]$.

Case 1 $D\perp(Y_0,Y_1)$.  $\beta_1=E[Y|D=1]-E[Y|D=0]=E[Y_1]-E[Y_0]=E[\tau]>0$. Unconditional randomisation gives the ATE and the sign is forced.

Case 2 $D\perp(Y_0,Y_1)|X$ but $X$ is omitted.  
$E[Y|D=1]-E[Y|D=0]=E[h(X)|D=1]+E[m_0(X)|D=1]-E[m_0(X)|D=0]$.  
$E[Cov(D,Y|X)]=E[Var(D|X)h(X)]>0$ but
$Cov(D,Y)=E[Cov(D,Y|X)]+Cov\!\big(p(X),m_0(X)+p(X)h(X)\big)$.
The selection term $Cov(p,m_0)$ is unrestricted by conditional randomisation. With $p(X)$ decreasing in $m_0(X)$, e.g. $X\in\{0,1\}$, $p_0=0.9$, $p_1=0.1$, $m_0(0)=0$, $m_0(1)=100$, $\tau\equiv1$, $E[Y|D=1]-E[Y|D=0]<0$ while $\tau>0$ a.s. The marginal $1,D$ OLS is not signed.

Case 3 linear projection of $Y$ on $1,D,X$.  Let $proj_{1,X}D=\alpha+\gamma X$, $v(X)=p(X)-\alpha-\gamma X$, $D_{\perp}=D-proj_{1,X}D$. Then
$E[D_{\perp}Y]=E[v(X)m_0(X)]+E[p(X)(1-\alpha-\gamma X)h(X)]$.
$E[(D-E[D|X])Y]=E[Var(D|X)h(X)]>0$ is the non-parametric partial covariance and is strictly positive. The linear residual replaces $E[D|X]$ by its linear projection. The term $E[v m_0]$ is the covariance of the linear-approximation error of $p$ with $m_0$ and is unrestricted by $D\perp(Y_0,\tau)|X$. It can be made arbitrarily negative by a non-linear $m_0$ and/or non-linear $p$.

E.g. $X\sim U[-1,1]$, $p(x)=\mathbf1\{x\ge0\}$, $proj_Xp(x)=\tfrac12+\tfrac34x$, $1-proj_Xp(x)<0$ for $x>2/3$, with $h(x)=e^{\lambda x}$, $\lambda\gg0$, gives $E[r_Dr_Y]<0$ while $h>0$ a.s. Or $X=1,2,3$ equiprobable, $m_0(x)=x^2$, $h\equiv0.1$, $p(1)=0.1$, $p(2)=0.9$, $p(3)=0.5$, gives $Cov(r_D,r_Y)<0$ although $E[Y|D=1,X]-E[Y|D=0,X]=h>0$ for every $X$.

Hence $Cov(Y,D|X)>0$ pointwise does not imply $Cov(Y_{\perp X},D_{\perp X})>0$ for the linear residual. Positivity holds for the non-parametric residual $D-E[D|X]$ but not for the linear residual $D-proj_{1,X}D$.

The E camp confuses the non-parametric partial effect $E[Var(D|X)h(X)]>0$ with the linear projection coefficient. The sign reversal is the classic linear Simpson reversal.

Current best assessment is therefore positivity is guaranteed only under unconditional randomisation. Cases 2 and 3 can both be sign reversed by $X$-dependent propensity scores and non-linear $m_0$/$p$. That is Answer A. Only Case 1.

6.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The problem is positivity of the population OLS slope of D in Y under τ_i = Y1i-Y0i >0 a.s.

Write Y = Y0 + D τ, m0(X)=E[Y0|X], h(X)=E[τ|X]>0 a.s., p(X)=E[D|X]. Under conditional randomisation D ⊥ (Y0,τ)|X so E[Y|X,D]=m0(X)+D h(X) and Cov(Y,D|X)=h(X)Var(D|X)>0 pointwise.

Case1: D ⊥ (Y0,Y1). Then β1 = E[Y|D=1]-E[Y|D=0]=E[Y1]-E[Y0]=E[τ]>0. Unconditional randomisation gives the ATE, strictly positive. All agree.

Case2: D ⊥ (Y0,Y1)|X but X omitted. 
E[Y|D=1]-E[Y|D=0]=E[h(X)|D=1]+E[m0(X)|D=1]-E[m0(X)|D=0].
The selection term E[m0|D=1]-E[m0|D=0]=Cov(p,m0)/Var(D) is unrestricted by unconfoundedness. With p(X) decreasing in m0(X) it can be arbitrarily negative and dominate E[h|D=1]. E.g. X∈{0,1}, p(0)=1,p(1)=0,m0(0)=0,m0(1)=100,τ≡0.1 gives E[Y|D=1]<E[Y|D=0] while τ>0 a.s. Hence the marginal difference in means, i.e. the OLS of Y on 1,D, is not signed.

Case3: D ⊥ (Y0,Y1)|X with linear control X. 
Let D̃=D-proj_{1,X}D, r(X)=p(X)-proj_{1,X}p(X). By law of total covariance
Cov(Y,D̃)=E[h(X)Var(D|X)]+Cov(m0(X)+p(X)h(X), r(X)).
The first term >0. The second term = E[r m0]+E[r p h] is unrestricted: r is the linear-approximation error of p, orthogonal to 1,X, and m0(X) is unrestricted given unconfoundedness. Choosing m0(X)=-k r(X)+linear part makes Cov(r,m0)=-k Var(r) arbitrarily negative. Hence Cov(Y,D̃) can be made <0 while h(X)>0 a.s. and D⊥(Y0,τ)|X.

Concrete examples: X~U[-1,1], p(x)=0.5+0.4x², m0(x)=-k x², h≡0.1 gives Cov(D,Y)∝-0.0356k+0.023<0 for large k; or three-point support X=1,2,3 with p(1)=0.1,p(2)=0.9,p(3)=0.5, m0=X², τ≡0.1 gives Cov(D̃,Y)<0. The same Simpson reversal occurs with m0 non-linear.

Thus Cov(Y,D|X)>0 pointwise does not imply Cov(Y,D̃)>0. The non-parametric residual D-E[D|X] has positive covariance E[h Var(D|X)]>0, but the linear residual D-proj_{1,X}D can pick up the non-linear part of m0 and reverse sign. That is the disagreement in the group: colleagues 1,5,6,7,8,9,13,14 claim the linear control restores positivity because E[Y|D=1,X]-E[Y|D=0,X]=h(X)>0. Colleagues 10,11,12,2,3,4 argue the linear projection is a misspecified approximation of m0(X)+p(X)h(X) and sign reversal is possible.

My current position remains the sign is guaranteed only under unconditional randomisation. Case2 is sign-unidentified by selection on X; Case3 is sign-unidentified by linear misspecification of m0 and p. Positivity of τ_i>0 a.s. forces positivity only in Case1. Unresolved tension remains with the E camp who conflate the conditional positive partial covariance Cov(Y,D|X)>0 with positivity of the linear projection coefficient β_D=Cov(Y,D̃)/Var(D̃).

2.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The model is $Y=Y_{0}+D\tau$, $\tau_i>0$ a.s., $m_{0}(X)=E[Y_{0}|X]$, $\tau(X)=E[\tau|X]>0$ a.s. and under conditional randomisation $D\perp(Y_{0},\tau)|X$ so $E[Y|X,D]=m_{0}(X)+D\tau(X)$ and $Cov(Y,D|X)=Var(D|X)\tau(X)>0$ for every $X$.

Case 1 $D\perp(Y_{0},Y_{1})$. Then $E[Y|D=1]-E[Y|D=0]=E[Y_{1}-Y_{0}]=E[\tau]>0$. The population OLS of $Y$ on $1,D$ is the ATE and the sign is forced.

Case 2 $D\perp(Y_{0},Y_{1})|X$ but $X$ omitted. 
$E[Y|D=1]-E[Y|D=0]=E[\tau(X)|D=1]+E[m_{0}(X)|D=1]-E[m_{0}(X)|D=0]$.
The selection term $E[m_{0}|D=1]-E[m_{0}|D=0]=Cov(p(X),m_{0}(X))/Var(D)$ is unrestricted. With $p(X)=P(D=1|X)$ decreasing in $m_{0}(X)$ it can dominate the positive $E[\tau|D=1]$ term, e.g. $X\in\{0,1\}$, $p(0)=1,p(1)=0$, $m_{0}(0)=0,m_{0}(1)=100$, $\tau\equiv0.1$ gives $E[Y|D=1]<E[Y|D=0]$ while $\tau_i>0$ a.s. Hence the marginal mean difference / OLS coefficient on $D$ without $X$ is sign-unidentified.

Case 3 linear projection $Y=a+bD+cX+u$. With Frisch-Waugh $b=Cov(D_{\perp X},Y)/Var(D_{\perp X})$ where $D_{\perp X}=D-{\rm proj}_{1,X}D$. Write $p(X)=a_{0}+a_{1}X+r(X)$, $E[r]=E[rX]=0$, so $D_{\perp X}=D-p(X)+r(X)$ and
$Cov(D_{\perp X},Y)=E[Var(D|X)\tau(X)]+Cov(r(X),m_{0}(X)+p(X)\tau(X))$.
The first term $E[Var(D|X)\tau(X)]>0$ is the non-parametric partial covariance. The second term is the covariance of the linear-approximation error of $p(X)$ with the linear-approximation error of $m_{0}(X)+p(X)\tau(X)$. Unconfoundedness does not restrict it. Because $m_{0}$ and $p$ are unrestricted non-linear functions of $X$, $Cov(r,m_{0})$ can be made arbitrarily negative and dominate the positive $E[Var(D|X)\tau(X)]$ term.

Explicit sign reversal: $X=1,2,3$ equiprobable, $m_{0}(x)=x^{2}$, $\tau\equiv0.1$, $p(1)=0.1,p(2)=0.9,p(3)=0.5$. Then ${\rm proj}_{1,X}p(x)=0.1+0.2x$, $r(x)=p(x)-{\rm proj}p(x)$ and $E[rE[Y|X]]<0$, so $b<0$ while $E[Y|D=1,X]-E[Y|D=0,X]=\tau>0$ for every $X$ and $\tau_i>0$ a.s. The same Simpson-type reversal works with $X\sim U[-1,1]$, $p(x)=0.5+0.4x^{2}$, $m_{0}(x)=-k x^{2}$, $\tau\equiv0.1$, giving $b\propto-0.0356k+0.023<0$ for $k\gtrsim1$.

Thus $Cov(Y,D|X)>0$ pointwise guarantees positivity of the non-parametric partial effect $E[(D-E[D|X])Y]=E[Var(D|X)\tau(X)]>0$, but it does not guarantee positivity of the linear projection coefficient on $D$ when $m_{0}$ and $p$ are non-linear. The E camp confuses the non-parametric residual $D-E[D|X]$ with the linear residual $D-{\rm proj}_{1,X}D$; $E[D_{\perp X}Y|X]=r(X)m_{0}(X)+\tau(X)E[D_{\perp X}D|X]\neq Var(D|X)\tau(X)$ in general.

So positivity of the individual effect forces positivity only under unconditional randomisation. Cases 2 and 3 can both be sign-reversed by a suitable non-linear $p(X)$ and $m_{0}(X)$ with $\tau_i>0$ a.s.

Current belief: guaranteed positivity holds only in Case 1, answer A. Only Case 1 and Case 2 must be positive is false; Only Case 1 and Case 3 must be positive is false under the stated non-parametric linear projection.

reflection_text.4:
The individual effect is $\tau_i=Y_{1i}-Y_{0i}>0$ a.s. and under
$D\perp(Y_{0},Y_{1})|X$

$E[Y|X,D]=m_{0}(X)+D\,h(X)$ with $m_{0}(X)=E[Y_{0}|X]$ and $h(X)=E[\tau|X]>0$ a.s.,
$p(X)=E[D|X]$, ${\rm Cov}(Y,D|X)=h(X){\rm Var}(D|X)>0$.

Case 1 $D\perp(Y_{0},Y_{1})$. Then
$\beta_{1}=E[Y|D=1]-E[Y|D=0]=E[Y_{1}]-E[Y_{0}]=E[\tau]>0$, the OLS slope is the ATE. Sign guaranteed.

Case 2 $D\perp(Y_{0},Y_{1})|X$ but $D$ is allowed to depend on $X$ and $X$ is omitted.
$E[Y|D=1]-E[Y|D=0]=E[h(X)|D=1]+E[m_{0}(X)|D=1]-E[m_{0}(X)|D=0]$.
The selection term $E[m_{0}|D=1]-E[m_{0}|D=0]$ is unrestricted by conditional randomisation.
With $p(X)$ decreasing in $m_{0}(X)$ the bias can dominate the positive $E[h|D=1]$ term.
E.g. $X\in\{0,1\}$, $p(0)=1,p(1)=0$, $m_{0}(0)=0,m_{0}(1)=100$, $\tau\equiv0.1$ gives $E[Y|D=1]<E[Y|D=0]$.
Hence the marginal difference in means, i.e. the $1,D$ OLS, is not signed.

Case 3 $1,D,X$ linear projection. Let $\tilde D=D-{\rm proj}_{1,X}D$, $v(X)=p(X)-{\rm proj}_{1,X}p(X)$.
Frisch–Waugh gives
${\rm Cov}(\tilde D,Y)=E[h(X){\rm Var}(D|X)]+{\rm Cov}\big(v(X),m_{0}(X)+p(X)h(X)\big)$.
The first term $E[h\,{\rm Var}(D|X)]>0$ is the non-parametric partial covariance.
The second term is the covariance of the linear-approximation error of $p(X)$ with the possibly non-linear baseline $m_{0}(X)+p(X)h(X)$. It is unrestricted by unconfoundedness and $h>0$.
With a non-linear $m_{0}$ and non-linear $p$ the term ${\rm Cov}(v,m_{0})$ can be made arbitrarily negative and dominate the positive $E[h\,{\rm Var}(D|X)]$ term.
Classic examples: $X\in\{-1,0,1\}$ equiprobable, $p(-1)=p(1)=0.9,p(0)=0.1$, $m_{0}(-1)=m_{0}(1)=0,m_{0}(0)=300$, $h\equiv1$ gives $E[Y|D,X]=m_{0}(X)+D$ strictly increasing in $D$ for every $X$ yet ${\rm Cov}(\tilde D,Y)<0$, so the linear coefficient on $D$ in $Y\sim1+D+X$ is negative. Similarly $X\sim U[-1,1]$, $p(x)=0.5+0.4x^{2}$, $m_{0}(x)=-k x^{2}$, $h\equiv0.1$ gives $\beta_{3}\propto-0.0356k+0.023<0$ for $k\gtrsim1$.

Hence $Cov(Y,D|X)>0$ pointwise does not imply $Cov(Y_{\perp X},D_{\perp X})>0$ for the linear residual $D_{\perp X}=D-{\rm proj}_{1,X}D$. The non-parametric partial effect $E[Var(D|X)h(X)]/E[Var(D|X)]>0$ is positive, but the linear projection can suffer sign reversal because the linear span $\{1,X\}$ does not span $m_{0}(X)$ and $p(X)$ in general; the residual $v(X)$ can proxy the non-linear part of $m_{0}$.

The colleagues arguing for E – Only Case 1 and Case 3 – conflate the non-parametric partial covariance with the linear projection coefficient. While $E[Y|D=1,X]-E[Y|D=0,X]=h(X)>0$ for every $X$ holds, the best linear approximation to $m_{0}(X)+D h(X)$ in the space $\{1,D,X\}$ need not be monotone in $D$ when $m_{0}$ and $p$ are non-linear. The sign guarantee survives the unconditional randomised case, and would survive a fully non-parametric control for $X$, but it does not survive a linear control for $X$.

Thus the only case where positivity of $\tau_i>0$ a.s. forces a positive population OLS coefficient on $D$ is unconditional randomisation. Cases 2 and 3 can both be sign-reversed by $X$-dependent propensity and non-linear $m_{0}$. Current best belief: A. Only Case 1.
reflection_text.12:
The individual effect is τ_i=Y1i−Y0i>0 a.s. and under conditional randomisation
E[Y|X,D]=m0(X)+D τ(X) with τ(X)=E[τ|X]>0, p(X)=E[D|X].

Case 1: D⊥(Y0,Y1). Then β1 =E[Y|D=1]−E[Y|D=0]=E[Y1]−E[Y0]=E[τ]>0.
Unconditional randomisation gives the ATE and the ordinary difference in means is strictly positive.

Case 2: D⊥(Y0,Y1)|X but D may depend on X.
E[Y|D=1]−E[Y|D=0]=E[τ(X)|D=1]+E[m0(X)|D=1]−E[m0(X)|D=0].
The first term >0 but the selection term E[m0(X)|D=1]−E[m0(X)|D=0] is unrestricted by unconfoundedness. With p(X) decreasing in m0(X) the bias can dominate the positive treatment term, e.g. X∈{0,1}, p0=1,p1=0, m0(0)=0,m0(1)=100, τ≡0.1 gives E[Y|D=1]=0.1<1=E[Y|D=0]. The marginal OLS coefficient need not be positive.

Case 3: Linear projection of Y on 1,D,X. Let proj_{1,X}D=α+βX and r(X)=p(X)−α−βX. Then
E[(D−α−βX)Y]=E[r(X)(m0(X)+τ(X)p(X))].
Cov(Y,D|X)=Var(D|X)τ(X)>0, but the linear residual r(X) is orthogonal only to 1,X, not to m0(X). Because m0(·) and p(·) can be non-linear the term E[r(X)m0(X)] can be made arbitrarily negative relative to the positive E[r(X)τ(X)p(X)].

A concrete discrete example shows reversal: X=1,2,3 equiprobable, p(1)=0.1,p(2)=0.9,p(3)=0.5, m0(X)=X², τ≡0.1>0. Then proj_{1,X}p=0.1+0.2X, r=−0.2,0.4,−0.2 and E[r(m0+τp)]<0, so the population Frisch-Waugh coefficient on D is negative while τ>0 a.s. and D⊥(Y0,Y1)|X. The linear X control soaks up only the linear part of m0 and p; the non-linear remainder can be used by D as a proxy for m0 and flip the sign. Same Simpson-type reversal with X∼U[-1,1], p(x)=0.5+0.4x², m0(x)=−k x² gives β∝−0.0356k+0.023<0 for k large.

Hence a strictly positive population OLS slope is guaranteed only under unconditional randomisation. Case 2 and the linearly controlled Case 3 can both be signed the wrong way by selection on X and by linear misspecification of m0(X). The E camp that claims Case 3 must be positive conflates the non-parametric partial covariance E[Var(D|X)τ(X)]>0 with the linear projection Cov(Y,D⊥X)>0. With only a linear term in X the projection residual D−proj_{1,X}D is not mean independent of m0(X), so positivity of the conditional mean in D does not imply positivity of the linear coefficient.

The split in the room between E Only Case1 and Case3 and A Only Case1 reflects the common confusion between conditional mean positivity Cov(Y,D|X)>0 and positivity of the linear projection coefficient when m0(X) is non-linear. The correct non-parametric conclusion with no parametric restriction on m0 is A.

Current belief remains A. Only Case 1 must be positive.
reflection_text.10:
The core model is Y = Y0 + D τ, τ>0 a.s., D ⟂ (Y0,τ) | X, so E[Y|X,D]=m0(X)+D h(X) with h(X)=E[τ|X]>0 a.s., p(X)=E[D|X]. 

Case 1 unconditional randomisation: β1 = E[Y|D=1]-E[Y|D=0]=E[τ]>0. Uncontroversial.

Case 2 marginal regression under conditional randomisation: 
E[Y|D=1]-E[Y|D=0]=E[h(X)|D=1]+E[m0(X)|D=1]-E[m0(X)|D=0].
The selection term E[m0|X]|D=1 - E[m0|X]|D=0 is unrestricted by D ⟂ (Y0,τ)|X. With p(X) decreasing in m0(X) the marginal difference in means can be made arbitrarily negative while τ>0 a.s., e.g. Y0=X, τ≡0.1, p(x)=1{x<0}. So the uncontrolled OLS slope is not sign identified.

Case 3 Y on 1,D,X is the linear projection. Let D̃ = D - proj_{1,X}D and r(X)=E[D̃|X]=p(X)-proj_{1,X}p(X). Then
Cov(Y,D̃)=E[Cov(Y,D|X)]+Cov(E[Y|X],r(X))
       =E[Var(D|X)h(X)]+Cov(m0(X)+p(X)h(X), r(X)).
The first term >0. The second term is the covariance of the linear-approximation error of p(X) with the linear-approximation error of m0(X)+p(X)h(X). Unconfoundedness does not restrict it. With a non-linear m0(·) and non-linear p(·) the term Cov(r(X),m0(X)) can be made arbitrarily negative and dominate E[Var(D|X)h(X)].

Explicit sign reversal: X∈{-1,0,1} equiprobable, m0(x)=x², h≡0.1, p(-1)=0.1,p(0)=0.9,p(1)=0.5. Then E[Y|X,D]=x²+0.1D is strictly increasing in D for every X, yet proj_{1,X}D is linear in X and Cov(D̃,Y)<0, giving Frisch-Waugh coefficient ≈-0.5<0 while τ>0 a.s. and D ⟂ (Y0,Y1)|X. Same construction works with continuous X, e.g. p(x)=0.5+0.4x², m0(x)=-k x², h≡0.1 giving β3∝-0.0356k+0.023<0 for k large.

Thus Cov(Y,D|X)>0 pointwise does not imply Cov(Y⊥X,D⊥X)>0 for the linear residuals. The non-parametric residual D-E[D|X] is guaranteed positive, but the linear residual D-proj_{1,X}D is not.

The E camp argues β3 = E[Var(D|X)h(X)]/E[Var(D|X)]>0 by partialling out X, i.e. using D-E[D|X] rather than D-proj_{1,X}D, and assumes the linear control removes the selection channel. That holds if m0(X) and p(X) are linear in X, but no such parametric restriction is given.

Hence positivity of the individual effect forces positivity only under unconditional randomisation. Under conditional randomisation the marginal slope Case 2 can be negative, and the linearly controlled slope Case 3 can also be negative by linear misspecification of m0(X) and p(X). Current belief remains A. Only Case 1.
reflection_text.3:
The population OLS coefficient is the linear projection of Y on the regressors.

Write Y = Y0 + D τ with τ>0 a.s. and under conditional randomisation
E[Y|X,D]= m0(X)+ D h(X) with m0(X)=E[Y0|X], h(X)=E[τ|X]>0,
p(X)=E[D|X], D⊥(Y0,τ)|X.

Case 1 D⊥(Y0,Y1). β1 = E[Y|D=1]-E[Y|D=0]=E[Y1]-E[Y0]=E[τ]>0.
Unconditional randomisation identifies the ATE and sign is guaranteed.

Case 2 D⊥(Y0,Y1)|X but regression is Y~1+D.
E[Y|D=1]-E[Y|D=0]=E[h(X)|D=1]+E[m0(X)|D=1]-E[m0(X)|D=0].
The selection term E[m0|D=1]-E[m0|D=0]=Cov(p,m0)/Var(D) is unrestricted.
With p(X) decreasing in m0(X) the bias can dominate E[h|D=1].
E.g. X∈{0,1}, p0=1,p1=0,m0(0)=0,m0(1)=100,τ≡0.1 gives
E[Y|D=1]=0.1<1=E[Y|D=0] although τ>0 a.s. Sign not guaranteed.

Case 3 Y~1+D+X linear projection.
Let D̃ = D - proj_{1,X} D, v(X)=p(X)-proj_{1,X}p(X), E[v]=E[vX]=0.
E[Y D̃|X]= v(X)[m0(X)+p(X)h(X)] + h(X)p(X)(1-p(X)).
Hence
Cov(Y,D̃)=E[h(X)p(X)(1-p(X))]+E[v(X)(m0(X)+p(X)h(X))].
First term >0. Second term =Cov(v, E[Y|X]) is unrestricted by unconfoundedness.
With m0 non-linear in X the linear space {1,X} does not span m0 and v can be made
negatively correlated with m0 + p h to dominate the positive first term.
E.g. X=1,2,3 equiprobable, m0(X)=X², h≡0.1, p(1)=0.1,p(2)=0.9,p(3)=0.5 gives
proj_{1,X}D linear in X and Cov(D̃,Y)<0 while E[Y|D=1,X]-E[Y|D=0,X]=h>0 a.s.
Same Simpson reversal with p(x)=0.5+0.4x², m0(x)=-k x².

Thus Cov(Y,D|X)=Var(D|X)h(X)>0 pointwise, so the non-parametric
partial effect is positive, but the linear projection onto {1,D,X} is not.
The E camp confuses the non-parametric residual D-E[D|X] with the linear
residual D-proj_{1,X}D and assumes Cov(D̃,m0)=0. Under conditional
randomisation Cov(D,m0|X)=0, but Cov(D̃,m0)≠0 when m0 is non-linear.

Positivity of τ_i>0 guarantees positivity of the unadjusted slope only
under unconditional randomisation. With conditional randomisation the
marginal slope in Case 2 and the linearly adjusted slope in Case 3 can both
be signed the wrong way by selection on X and by linear misspecification
of E[Y0|X]. Consensus in the deliberation is split, with a minority claiming
Case 3 is guaranteed by E[Y|D=1,X]-E[Y|D=0,X]>0. That claim holds for the
non-parametric partial regression, not for the population linear projection
Y~1+D+X with unrestricted m0.

Current belief: sign is guaranteed only in Case 1. Option A. Only Case 1 and Case 3 remain disputed; the error is the linear vs non-parametric residual distinction.
reflection_text.11:

E[D̃|X]=p(X)-a-bX ≠0 unless p linear. 
E[D̃ Y|X]=E[D̃|X]E[Y|X]+Var(D|X)h(X).
Hence E[D̃ Y]=E[E[D̃|X]E[Y|X]]+E[Var(D|X)h(X)].
Second term >0. First term = E[(p-proj p)(m0+ph)] can be made arbitrarily negative by non-linear p and m0.
Indeed with E[D̃|X]=p-a-bX, 
E[D̃Y|X]=E[D̃|X](m0+ p h)+p(1-p)h.
The term E[D̃|X](m0+ph) is unrestricted by unconfoundedness. 
Explicit three-point example X=1,2,3 equiprobable, m0(x)=x², h≡0.1, p(1)=0.1,p(2)=0.9,p(3)=0.5 gives proj p linear, Cov(D̃,Y)<0 while h>0 a.s. and E[Y|D=1,X]-E[Y|D=0,X]=h>0 for every X. 
The same reversal occurs with p(x)=0.5+0.4x², m0(x)=-k x², h≡0.1 giving β∝ -0.0356k+0.023, negative for k large.

Thus Cov(Y,D|X)>0 pointwise does not imply Cov(Y,D̃)>0 for linear residual. The E camp argues E[D̃ Y|X]=Var(D|X)h>0, which uses the non-parametric residual D-E[D|X] where E[D̃|X]=0. With linear projection E[D̃|X]≠0, the extra term E[E[D̃|X]E[Y|X]] can flip sign.

So positivity of individual effect guarantees positivity of unconditional randomised mean difference, but not of the marginal mean difference under conditional randomisation, nor of the linearly controlled projection. The only guaranteed case is Case 1.

Current belief: A. Only Case 1. Cases 2 and 3 can be sign reversed by selection on X and by linear misspecification of m0 and p.
reflection_text.8:
The model is $Y=Y_{0}+D\tau$, $\tau_i>0$ a.s., $E[Y|X,D]=m_0(X)+D\,h(X)$ with $h(X)=E[\tau|X]>0$ a.s. and $D\perp(Y_0,\tau)|X$, $p(X)=E[D|X]$.

Case 1 $D\perp(Y_0,Y_1)$.  $\beta_1=E[Y|D=1]-E[Y|D=0]=E[Y_1]-E[Y_0]=E[\tau]>0$. Unconditional randomisation gives the ATE and the sign is forced.

Case 2 $D\perp(Y_0,Y_1)|X$ but $X$ is omitted.  
$E[Y|D=1]-E[Y|D=0]=E[h(X)|D=1]+E[m_0(X)|D=1]-E[m_0(X)|D=0]$.  
$E[Cov(D,Y|X)]=E[Var(D|X)h(X)]>0$ but
$Cov(D,Y)=E[Cov(D,Y|X)]+Cov\!\big(p(X),m_0(X)+p(X)h(X)\big)$.
The selection term $Cov(p,m_0)$ is unrestricted by conditional randomisation. With $p(X)$ decreasing in $m_0(X)$, e.g. $X\in\{0,1\}$, $p_0=0.9$, $p_1=0.1$, $m_0(0)=0$, $m_0(1)=100$, $\tau\equiv1$, $E[Y|D=1]-E[Y|D=0]<0$ while $\tau>0$ a.s. The marginal $1,D$ OLS is not signed.

Case 3 linear projection of $Y$ on $1,D,X$.  Let $proj_{1,X}D=\alpha+\gamma X$, $v(X)=p(X)-\alpha-\gamma X$, $D_{\perp}=D-proj_{1,X}D$. Then
$E[D_{\perp}Y]=E[v(X)m_0(X)]+E[p(X)(1-\alpha-\gamma X)h(X)]$.
$E[(D-E[D|X])Y]=E[Var(D|X)h(X)]>0$ is the non-parametric partial covariance and is strictly positive. The linear residual replaces $E[D|X]$ by its linear projection. The term $E[v m_0]$ is the covariance of the linear-approximation error of $p$ with $m_0$ and is unrestricted by $D\perp(Y_0,\tau)|X$. It can be made arbitrarily negative by a non-linear $m_0$ and/or non-linear $p$.

E.g. $X\sim U[-1,1]$, $p(x)=\mathbf1\{x\ge0\}$, $proj_Xp(x)=\tfrac12+\tfrac34x$, $1-proj_Xp(x)<0$ for $x>2/3$, with $h(x)=e^{\lambda x}$, $\lambda\gg0$, gives $E[r_Dr_Y]<0$ while $h>0$ a.s. Or $X=1,2,3$ equiprobable, $m_0(x)=x^2$, $h\equiv0.1$, $p(1)=0.1$, $p(2)=0.9$, $p(3)=0.5$, gives $Cov(r_D,r_Y)<0$ although $E[Y|D=1,X]-E[Y|D=0,X]=h>0$ for every $X$.

Hence $Cov(Y,D|X)>0$ pointwise does not imply $Cov(Y_{\perp X},D_{\perp X})>0$ for the linear residual. Positivity holds for the non-parametric residual $D-E[D|X]$ but not for the linear residual $D-proj_{1,X}D$.

The E camp confuses the non-parametric partial effect $E[Var(D|X)h(X)]>0$ with the linear projection coefficient. The sign reversal is the classic linear Simpson reversal.

Current best assessment is therefore positivity is guaranteed only under unconditional randomisation. Cases 2 and 3 can both be sign reversed by $X$-dependent propensity scores and non-linear $m_0$/$p$. That is Answer A. Only Case 1.
reflection_text.6:
The problem is positivity of the population OLS slope of D in Y under τ_i = Y1i-Y0i >0 a.s.

Write Y = Y0 + D τ, m0(X)=E[Y0|X], h(X)=E[τ|X]>0 a.s., p(X)=E[D|X]. Under conditional randomisation D ⊥ (Y0,τ)|X so E[Y|X,D]=m0(X)+D h(X) and Cov(Y,D|X)=h(X)Var(D|X)>0 pointwise.

Case1: D ⊥ (Y0,Y1). Then β1 = E[Y|D=1]-E[Y|D=0]=E[Y1]-E[Y0]=E[τ]>0. Unconditional randomisation gives the ATE, strictly positive. All agree.

Case2: D ⊥ (Y0,Y1)|X but X omitted. 
E[Y|D=1]-E[Y|D=0]=E[h(X)|D=1]+E[m0(X)|D=1]-E[m0(X)|D=0].
The selection term E[m0|D=1]-E[m0|D=0]=Cov(p,m0)/Var(D) is unrestricted by unconfoundedness. With p(X) decreasing in m0(X) it can be arbitrarily negative and dominate E[h|D=1]. E.g. X∈{0,1}, p(0)=1,p(1)=0,m0(0)=0,m0(1)=100,τ≡0.1 gives E[Y|D=1]<E[Y|D=0] while τ>0 a.s. Hence the marginal difference in means, i.e. the OLS of Y on 1,D, is not signed.

Case3: D ⊥ (Y0,Y1)|X with linear control X. 
Let D̃=D-proj_{1,X}D, r(X)=p(X)-proj_{1,X}p(X). By law of total covariance
Cov(Y,D̃)=E[h(X)Var(D|X)]+Cov(m0(X)+p(X)h(X), r(X)).
The first term >0. The second term = E[r m0]+E[r p h] is unrestricted: r is the linear-approximation error of p, orthogonal to 1,X, and m0(X) is unrestricted given unconfoundedness. Choosing m0(X)=-k r(X)+linear part makes Cov(r,m0)=-k Var(r) arbitrarily negative. Hence Cov(Y,D̃) can be made <0 while h(X)>0 a.s. and D⊥(Y0,τ)|X.

Concrete examples: X~U[-1,1], p(x)=0.5+0.4x², m0(x)=-k x², h≡0.1 gives Cov(D,Y)∝-0.0356k+0.023<0 for large k; or three-point support X=1,2,3 with p(1)=0.1,p(2)=0.9,p(3)=0.5, m0=X², τ≡0.1 gives Cov(D̃,Y)<0. The same Simpson reversal occurs with m0 non-linear.

Thus Cov(Y,D|X)>0 pointwise does not imply Cov(Y,D̃)>0. The non-parametric residual D-E[D|X] has positive covariance E[h Var(D|X)]>0, but the linear residual D-proj_{1,X}D can pick up the non-linear part of m0 and reverse sign. That is the disagreement in the group: colleagues 1,5,6,7,8,9,13,14 claim the linear control restores positivity because E[Y|D=1,X]-E[Y|D=0,X]=h(X)>0. Colleagues 10,11,12,2,3,4 argue the linear projection is a misspecified approximation of m0(X)+p(X)h(X) and sign reversal is possible.

My current position remains the sign is guaranteed only under unconditional randomisation. Case2 is sign-unidentified by selection on X; Case3 is sign-unidentified by linear misspecification of m0 and p. Positivity of τ_i>0 a.s. forces positivity only in Case1. Unresolved tension remains with the E camp who conflate the conditional positive partial covariance Cov(Y,D|X)>0 with positivity of the linear projection coefficient β_D=Cov(Y,D̃)/Var(D̃).
reflection_text.2:
The model is $Y=Y_{0}+D\tau$, $\tau_i>0$ a.s., $m_{0}(X)=E[Y_{0}|X]$, $\tau(X)=E[\tau|X]>0$ a.s. and under conditional randomisation $D\perp(Y_{0},\tau)|X$ so $E[Y|X,D]=m_{0}(X)+D\tau(X)$ and $Cov(Y,D|X)=Var(D|X)\tau(X)>0$ for every $X$.

Case 1 $D\perp(Y_{0},Y_{1})$. Then $E[Y|D=1]-E[Y|D=0]=E[Y_{1}-Y_{0}]=E[\tau]>0$. The population OLS of $Y$ on $1,D$ is the ATE and the sign is forced.

Case 2 $D\perp(Y_{0},Y_{1})|X$ but $X$ omitted. 
$E[Y|D=1]-E[Y|D=0]=E[\tau(X)|D=1]+E[m_{0}(X)|D=1]-E[m_{0}(X)|D=0]$.
The selection term $E[m_{0}|D=1]-E[m_{0}|D=0]=Cov(p(X),m_{0}(X))/Var(D)$ is unrestricted. With $p(X)=P(D=1|X)$ decreasing in $m_{0}(X)$ it can dominate the positive $E[\tau|D=1]$ term, e.g. $X\in\{0,1\}$, $p(0)=1,p(1)=0$, $m_{0}(0)=0,m_{0}(1)=100$, $\tau\equiv0.1$ gives $E[Y|D=1]<E[Y|D=0]$ while $\tau_i>0$ a.s. Hence the marginal mean difference / OLS coefficient on $D$ without $X$ is sign-unidentified.

Case 3 linear projection $Y=a+bD+cX+u$. With Frisch-Waugh $b=Cov(D_{\perp X},Y)/Var(D_{\perp X})$ where $D_{\perp X}=D-{\rm proj}_{1,X}D$. Write $p(X)=a_{0}+a_{1}X+r(X)$, $E[r]=E[rX]=0$, so $D_{\perp X}=D-p(X)+r(X)$ and
$Cov(D_{\perp X},Y)=E[Var(D|X)\tau(X)]+Cov(r(X),m_{0}(X)+p(X)\tau(X))$.
The first term $E[Var(D|X)\tau(X)]>0$ is the non-parametric partial covariance. The second term is the covariance of the linear-approximation error of $p(X)$ with the linear-approximation error of $m_{0}(X)+p(X)\tau(X)$. Unconfoundedness does not restrict it. Because $m_{0}$ and $p$ are unrestricted non-linear functions of $X$, $Cov(r,m_{0})$ can be made arbitrarily negative and dominate the positive $E[Var(D|X)\tau(X)]$ term.

Explicit sign reversal: $X=1,2,3$ equiprobable, $m_{0}(x)=x^{2}$, $\tau\equiv0.1$, $p(1)=0.1,p(2)=0.9,p(3)=0.5$. Then ${\rm proj}_{1,X}p(x)=0.1+0.2x$, $r(x)=p(x)-{\rm proj}p(x)$ and $E[rE[Y|X]]<0$, so $b<0$ while $E[Y|D=1,X]-E[Y|D=0,X]=\tau>0$ for every $X$ and $\tau_i>0$ a.s. The same Simpson-type reversal works with $X\sim U[-1,1]$, $p(x)=0.5+0.4x^{2}$, $m_{0}(x)=-k x^{2}$, $\tau\equiv0.1$, giving $b\propto-0.0356k+0.023<0$ for $k\gtrsim1$.

Thus $Cov(Y,D|X)>0$ pointwise guarantees positivity of the non-parametric partial effect $E[(D-E[D|X])Y]=E[Var(D|X)\tau(X)]>0$, but it does not guarantee positivity of the linear projection coefficient on $D$ when $m_{0}$ and $p$ are non-linear. The E camp confuses the non-parametric residual $D-E[D|X]$ with the linear residual $D-{\rm proj}_{1,X}D$; $E[D_{\perp X}Y|X]=r(X)m_{0}(X)+\tau(X)E[D_{\perp X}D|X]\neq Var(D|X)\tau(X)$ in general.

So positivity of the individual effect forces positivity only under unconditional randomisation. Cases 2 and 3 can both be sign-reversed by a suitable non-linear $p(X)$ and $m_{0}(X)$ with $\tau_i>0$ a.s.

Current belief: guaranteed positivity holds only in Case 1, answer A. Only Case 1 and Case 2 must be positive is false; Only Case 1 and Case 3 must be positive is false under the stated non-parametric linear projection.

4.text:
With $Y=Y_{0}+D\tau$, $\tau_{i}>0$ a.s., $m_{0}(X)=E[Y_{0}|X]$,
$h(X)=E[\tau|X]>0$ a.s. and $D\perp(Y_{0},\tau)|X$,

$E[Y|X,D]=m_{0}(X)+h(X)D$,      $p(X)=E[D|X]$,
${\rm Cov}(Y,D|X)=h(X){\rm Var}(D|X)>0$
pointwise, and the non-parametric partial effect
$E[{\rm Var}(D|X)h(X)]/E[{\rm Var}(D|X)]>0$.

* Case 1. $D\perp(Y_{0},Y_{1})$.
$$
\beta_{1}=E[Y|D=1]-E[Y|D=0]=E[Y_{1}]-E[Y_{0}]=E[\tau]>0,
$$
the OLS slope is the ATE. The sign is forced.

* Case 2. $D\perp(Y_{0},Y_{1})|X$ but $X$ is omitted.
$$
E[Y|D=1]-E[Y|D=0]=E[h(X)|D=1]+E[m_{0}(X)|D=1]-E[m_{0}(X)|D=0].
$$
The selection term $E[m_{0}|D=1]-E[m_{0}|D=0]$ is unrestricted by
unconfoundedness. With $p(X)$ decreasing in $m_{0}(X)$ it can dominate the
positive $E[h|D=1]$ term. E.g. $X\in\{0,1\}$, $p(0)=1,p(1)=0$,
$m_{0}(0)=0,m_{0}(1)=100$, $\tau\equiv0.1$ gives
$E[Y|D=1]=0.1<1=E[Y|D=0]$ although $\tau_{i}>0$ a.s. The marginal
$1,D$ projection is not sign identified.

* Case 3. $Y$ on $1,D,X$ is the linear projection.
Let $\tilde D=D-{\rm proj}_{1,X}D$, $v(X)=p(X)-{\rm proj}_{1,X}p(X)$.
Frisch-Waugh gives
$$
{\rm Cov}(\tilde D,Y)=E\big[{\rm Var}(D|X)h(X)\big]
+{\rm Cov}\!\big(v(X),m_{0}(X)+p(X)h(X)\big).
$$
The first term is $>0$, the second is the covariance of the linear
approximation error of $p(X)$ with the possibly non-linear function
$m_{0}(X)+p(X)h(X)$. It is unrestricted by $D\perp(Y_{0},\tau)|X$.
Hence $ {\rm Cov}(Y,D|X)>0$ pointwise does not imply
${\rm Cov}(\tilde D,Y)>0$.

For example $X\in\{-1,0,1\}$ equiprobable,
$p(-1)=p(1)=0.9$, $p(0)=0.1$, $m_{0}(x)=-k x^{2}$,
$h\equiv1$. Then ${\rm proj}_{1,X}p$ is constant, $v(-1)=v(1)>0$,
$v(0)<0$, $E[Y|X,D]=m_{0}(X)+D$ is strictly increasing in $D$ for every
$X$, yet

${\rm Cov}(\tilde D,Y)=E[v m_{0}]+E[pv]>0$ is $>0$ for $k=0$ and
becomes $<0$ for $k$ large enough. The Frisch-Waugh coefficient

$\beta_{3}= {\rm Cov}(\tilde D,Y)/{\rm Var}(\tilde D)$

is negative while $E[Y|D=1,X]-E[Y|D=0,X]=h(X)>0$ a.s. The same
Simpson-type reversal is obtained with $X\sim U[-1,1]$,
$p(x)=0.5+0.4x^{2}$, $m_{0}(x)=-kx^{2}$, $h\equiv0.1$, for which
$\beta_{3}\propto-0.0356k+0.023<0$ for $k\gtrsim1$.

The linear span $\{1,X\}$ does not span $m_{0}(X)$ and $p(X)$ in general,
so the residual $v(X)$ can proxy the non-linear part of $m_{0}$
and reverse the sign. Positivity of the individual effect forces positivity
of the unconditionally randomised difference in means, and of the
non-parametric partial covariance $E[{\rm Var}(D|X)h(X)]$, but it does
not force positivity of the linear projection on $1,D,X$.

Hence the sign is forced only under unconditional randomisation.

A. Only Case 1

6.text:
The population OLS coefficient is the linear projection of $Y$ on the regressors. 
Write $Y=Y_{0}+D\tau$, $\tau>0$ a.s., $m_{0}(X)=E[Y_{0}|X]$, $h(X)=E[\tau|X]>0$ a.s.
and $p(X)=E[D|X]$. Under conditional randomisation

$E[Y|X,D]=m_{0}(X)+h(X)D$,

so $Cov(Y,D|X)=Var(D|X)h(X)>0$ pointwise, i.e. the non-parametric partial
effect is strictly positive.

*Case 1.* $D\perp(Y_{0},Y_{1})$. Then 
$\beta_{1}=E[Y|D=1]-E[Y|D=0]=E[Y_{1}]-E[Y_{0}]=E[\tau]>0$.
The constant-$D$ OLS is the ATE and is strictly positive.

*Case 2.* $D\perp(Y_{0},Y_{1})|X$ but $X$ is omitted.
\begin{equation*}
E[Y|D=1]-E[Y|D=0]=E[h(X)|D=1]+E[m_{0}(X)|D=1]-E[m_{0}(X)|D=0].
\end{equation*}
The first term $>0$ but $E[m_{0}|D=1]-E[m_{0}|D=0]=Cov(p,m_{0})/Var(D)$ is
unrestricted by unconfoundedness.  With $p(x)$ decreasing in $m_{0}(x)$
the selection bias can dominate $E[h|D=1]$, e.g. $X\in\{0,1\}$,
$p(0)=1,p(1)=0$, $m_{0}(0)=0,m_{0}(1)=100$, $\tau\equiv0.1$, gives
$E[Y|D=1]=0.1<1=E[Y|D=0]$ while $\tau_{i}>0$ a.s. The marginal
$1,D$ regression is not signed.

*Case 3.*  The linear projection is
$\beta_{D}=Cov(\tilde D,Y)/Var(\tilde D)$ with $\tilde D=D-proj_{1,X}D$.
Let $p(x)=a_{0}+a_{1}x+r(x)$, $E[r]=E[rX]=0$. Then

$Cov(\tilde D,Y)=E[Var(D|X)h(X)]+Cov(r(X),m_{0}(X)+p(X)h(X))$.

The first term $>0$, the second term is the covariance of the linear
approximation error of $p$ with the linear approximation error of
$m_{0}+ph$ and is unrestricted by $D\perp(Y_{0},\tau)|X$.
$Cov(Y,D|X)>0$ does not imply $Cov(Y,\tilde D)>0$: the linear residual
$\tilde D$ can proxy the non-linear part of $m_{0}$.

E.g. $X\in\{1,2,3\}$ equiprob., $m_{0}(x)=x^{2}$, $h\equiv0.1$,
$p(1)=0.1,p(2)=0.9,p(3)=0.5$.  Then $E[Y|X,D]=x^{2}+0.1D$ is strictly
increasing in $D$ for every $X$, yet $proj_{1,X}p=0.1+0.2X$,
$r=-0.2,0.4,-0.2$ and
$E[rE[Y|X]]=\frac13[-0.2(1.01)+0.4(4.09)-0.2(9.05)]<0$,
so $Cov(\tilde D,Y)<0$ and $\beta_{D}<0$ in the population regression
$Y=\alpha+\beta_{D}D+\gamma X+u$ while $\tau_{i}>0$ a.s. and
$D\perp(Y_{0},Y_{1})|X$.

Hence $Cov(Y,D|X)>0$ pointwise, and the non-parametric partial effect
$E[Y|D=1,X]-E[Y|D=0,X]=h(X)>0$, does not imply positivity of the linear
projection onto $\{1,D,X\}$. Positivity of the individual effect forces
positivity only under unconditional randomisation.

A. Only Case 1.

7.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I think the E reading is the one that matches the economics of the problem.

Case 1 is clear. Unconditional randomisation gives D ⟂ Y0,Y1 so
E[Y|D=1]−E[Y|D=0]=E[Y1−Y0]=E[τ]>0. The OLS of Y on 1,D is the ATE and it is strictly positive with τi>0 a.s.

Case 2 is the classic omitted-X problem under conditional randomisation. With D ⟂ Y0,Y1|X
E[Y|X,D]=m0(X)+D h(X), h(X)=E[τ|X]>0 a.s.,
so
E[Y|D=1]−E[Y|D=0]=E[h(X)|D=1]+E[m0(X)|D=1]−E[m0(X)|D=0].
The first term is >0 but the second term is selection on baseline income. With a jobs programme targeted at low pre-income, p(X)=P(D=1|X) decreasing in m0(X), we can have E[m0(X)|D=1]<E[m0(X)|D=0] by an amount that dominates the positive treatment term. The marginal difference in means, and hence the population OLS of Y on 1,D, can be zero or negative even though E[Y|D=1,X]−E[Y|D=0,X]=h(X)>0 for every X. That is why Case 2 is not sign identified.

Once X is in the regression the selection channel is closed. Conditional on X the conditional mean is
E[Y|X,D]=m0(X)+D h(X) with h(X)>0 a.s. and D ⟂ Y0,Y1|X.
Hence for every X
E[Y|D=1,X]−E[Y|D=0,X]=h(X)>0 and Cov(Y,D|X)=Var(D|X)h(X)>0.

Let rD=D−proj_{1,X}D and rY=Y−proj_{1,X}Y. By Frisch-Waugh
β3=Cov(rD,rY)/Var(rD). Because E[rD|X]=0,
E[rD Y|X]=E[rD E[Y|X,D]|X]=E[rD D|X]h(X)=Var(D|X)h(X)>0,
so in population
Cov(rD,rY)=E[Var(D|X)h(X)]>0.
Var(rD)=E[Var(D|X)]>0. Thus β3 is a positive weighted average of the strictly positive conditional average treatment effects h(X)=E[τ|X].

In words, after partialling out the linear part of pre-income the residual variation in D is still positively correlated with Y because within each X stratum D is randomised and the conditional mean is monotone increasing in D. The linear control removes the X-induced selection that can flip the sign in Case 2.

The alleged sign reversals for the linearly controlled regression all rely on making proj_{1,X}p(X) a very poor approximation to p(X), i.e. on putting all of the non-linear part of m0(X) into the residual D⊥X and on letting proj_{1,X}p(X) leave the [0,1] interval where h(X) is largest so that the effective weight on h(X) becomes negative. With a binary D and a real income X that is plausibly bounded and with a propensity that stays in [0,1], the linear projection error v(X)=p(X)−proj_{1,X}p(X) has mean zero and is bounded. The covariance term E[v(X)m0(X)] is then the covariance of the approximation error of the propensity with the baseline mean; under conditional randomisation D⊥Y0|X the only source of residual covariance between rD and Y is Var(D|X)h(X)>0. The linear projection therefore preserves the point-wise monotonicity E[Y|D=1,X]>E[Y|D=0,X] for every X.

Hence positivity is guaranteed under unconditional randomisation, Case 1, and under conditional randomisation once X is linearly controlled, Case 3. It is not guaranteed for the uncontrolled marginal regression under conditional randomisation, Case 2.

Only Case 1 and Case 3.

5.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I’m with the E view – the sign is forced in the unconditionally randomised regression and in the regression that controls for X, but not in the uncontrolled regression under conditional randomisation.

Case 1 is textbook. $D\perp Y_{0},Y_{1}$ so $E[Y|D=1]-E[Y|D=0]=E[Y_{1}-Y_{0}]=E[\tau]>0$. The constant-$D$ OLS is the ATE and it is strictly positive with $\tau_i>0$ a.s.

Case 2 is $D\perp Y_{0},Y_{1}|X$ but $X$ is omitted. With $p(x)=P(D=1|X=x)$, $m_{0}(x)=E[Y_{0}|X=x]$ and $h(x)=E[\tau|X=x]>0$,
$E[Y|D=1]-E[Y|D=0]=E[h(X)|D=1]+E[m_{0}(X)|D=1]-E[m_{0}(X)|D=0]$.
The first term is $>0$ but the second term is pure selection on baseline income. If the programme is targeted at low $X$, $p(x)$ is decreasing in $m_{0}(x)$ and $E[m_{0}(X)|D=1]-E[m_{0}(X)|D=0]$ can dominate $E[h(X)|D=1]$. The marginal difference in means, and hence the OLS coefficient on $D$ without $X$, can be zero or negative even though $E[Y|D=1,X]-E[Y|D=0,X]=h(X)>0$ for every $X$. That is the usual omitted-$X$ bias.

Once $X$ is in the regression the selection channel is closed. Under unconfoundedness
$E[Y|X,D]=m_{0}(X)+D\,h(X)$ with $h(X)>0$ a.s. and $D\perp Y_{0},Y_{1}|X$, so
$Cov(Y,D|X)=Var(D|X)h(X)>0$ for every $X$ with $0<p(X)<1$.
In particular $E[Y|D=1,X]-E[Y|D=0,X]=h(X)>0$ pointwise.

Let $r_{D}=D-\operatorname{proj}_{1,X}D$ be the $1,X$-residual of $D$. Then
$E[r_{D}Y|X]=E[r_{D}E[Y|X,D]|X]=E[r_{D}D|X]h(X)=Var(D|X)h(X)>0$,
so
$Cov(Y,r_{D})=E[Var(D|X)h(X)]>0$ and $Var(r_{D})=E[Var(D|X)]>0$.
Hence by Frisch-Waugh
$\beta_{3}=Cov(Y,r_{D})/Var(r_{D})$ is a positive weighted average of the strictly positive conditional average effects $h(X)=E[\tau|X]$.
Controlling for pre-treatment income removes the $X$-induced selection that can flip the sign in Case 2 and leaves a residual association that is monotone in $D$ within each $X$ stratum.

The sign-reversal examples quoted for Case 3 rely on making the linear approximation error of $p(X)$ large enough that $\operatorname{proj}_{1,X}p$ leaves $[0,1]$ and the residual $v(X)=p(X)-\operatorname{proj}_{1,X}p(X)$ is artificially correlated with the non-linear part of $m_{0}(X)$. That is an extrapolation pathology of the linear projection, not a consequence of $D\perp Y_{0},Y_{1}|X$ together with $\tau_i>0$. Under conditional randomisation the only source of covariance between the $X$-residual of $D$ and $Y$ is $Var(D|X)h(X)>0$. Once $X$ is linearly controlled the best linear approximation to the strictly increasing conditional mean $m_{0}(X)+D h(X)$ must load $D$ with a positive sign.

So positivity is guaranteed under unconditional randomisation, Case 1, and under conditional randomisation once $X$ is controlled for, Case 3, but it is not guaranteed for the marginal regression under conditional randomisation, Case 2. That is Only Case 1 and Case 3.

9.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: E. Only Case 1 and Case 3

Case 1 is unconditional randomisation. $D\perp Y_{0},Y_{1}$ so
$E[Y|D=1]-E[Y|D=0]=E[Y_{1}-Y_{0}]=E[\tau]>0$ and the constant-$D$ OLS is the ATE. That sign is forced.

Case 2 is randomisation conditional on $X$ but $X$ is omitted from the regression. Under unconfoundedness
$E[Y|X,D]=m_{0}(X)+D\,h(X)$ with $m_{0}(X)=E[Y_{0}|X]$ and $h(X)=E[\tau|X]>0$ a.s.
Hence 
$E[Y|D=1]-E[Y|D=0]=E[h(X)|D=1]+E[m_{0}(X)|D=1]-E[m_{0}(X)|D=0]$.
The first term is $>0$ but $E[m_{0}(X)|D=1]-E[m_{0}(X)|D=0]$ is ordinary selection on baseline income. With $p(X)=P(D=1|X)$ decreasing in $m_{0}(X)$ the treated can have a lower mean baseline than the controls and the selection bias can dominate $E[h(X)|D=1]$. The marginal difference in means, i.e. the OLS coefficient on $D$ without $X$, is therefore not signed. That is the usual omitted-$X$ problem.

Once $X$ is entered the selection channel is closed. Conditional on $X$,
$E[Y|D=1,X]-E[Y|D=0,X]=h(X)>0$ a.s. and
${\rm Cov}(Y,D|X)={\rm Var}(D|X)h(X)>0$ whenever $0<p(X)<1$.
Write $r_{D}=D-{\rm proj}_{1,X}D$, $r_{Y}=Y-{\rm proj}_{1,X}Y$. By Frisch-Waugh
$\beta_{D}= {\rm Cov}(r_{D},r_{Y})/{\rm Var}(r_{D})$.
Because $E[r_{D}|X]=0$,
$E[r_{D}Y|X]=E[r_{D}E[Y|X,D]|X]=E[r_{D}D|X]h(X)={\rm Var}(D|X)h(X)>0$,
and $r_{D}$ is mean independent of any function of $X$. Hence
${\rm Cov}(r_{D},Y_{0})=E[r_{D}E[Y_{0}|X]]=0$ and
$E[r_{D}Y]=E[{\rm Var}(D|X)h(X)]>0$.
The denominator ${\rm Var}(r_{D})=E[{\rm Var}(D|X)]+{\rm Var}\!\big({\rm proj}_{1,X}p(X)\big)>0$.
So
$\beta_{D}=E[{\rm Var}(D|X)h(X)]/E[{\rm Var}(r_{D})]>0$, 
a positive weighted average of the strictly positive conditional average effects $h(X)=E[\tau|X]$.

In words, after partialling out the linear part of $X$ the residual variation in $D$ is still the within-$X$ randomisation variation. Within each $X$ stratum $D$ is randomised and $Y$ is monotone increasing in $D$. Controlling for pre-treatment income removes the $X$-induced selection that can flip the sign in Case 2 and leaves a residual association that must be positive when $\tau_{i}>0$ a.s.

The sign-reversal constructions that are quoted for Case 3 rely on treating $m_{0}(X)$ as being able to remain in the $D$ residual after linear projection of $X$. PUBLIC RESPONSE: E. Only Case 1 and Case 3

Case 1 is uncontroversial. Unconditional randomisation gives D ⟂ Y0,Y1 so
E[Y|D=1]-E[Y|D=0]=E[Y1]-E[Y0]=E[τ]>0 and the population OLS of Y on 1,D is the ATE. With τi>0 a.s. the slope is strictly positive.

Case 2 is not guaranteed. With D ⟂ Y0,Y1 | X but X omitted,
E[Y|D=1]-E[Y|D=0]=E[τ(X)|D=1]+E[m0(X)|D=1]-E[m0(X)|D=0]
with m0(X)=E[Y0|X]. The first term is >0 but the second term is selection on pre-treatment income. If P(D=1|X) is decreasing in m0(X) the treated have a lower mean baseline and the bias can dominate E[τ(X)|D=1]. That is the usual omitted-X sign reversal and everyone agrees on it.

Case 3 restores the sign. Under unconfoundedness
E[Y|X,D]=m0(X)+D h(X),   h(X)=E[τ|X]>0 a.s.,
and D ⟂ Y0,τ | X. Hence pointwise
E[Y|D=1,X]-E[Y|D=0,X]=h(X)>0
and
Cov(Y,D|X)=Var(D|X) h(X)>0
whenever Var(D|X)>0.

Write the Frisch-Waugh residual ṼD = D - proj_{1,X}D. Then
E[Y ṼD | X]=E[ṼD E[Y|X,D]|X]=E[ṼD D|X] h(X)=Var(D|X) h(X)>0,
so that after integrating over X
Cov(Y,ṼD)=E[Var(D|X) h(X)]>0.
With a genuine propensity score p(X)=E[D|X]∈[0,1] the linear predictor
proj_{1,X}D = proj_{1,X}p(X) stays in the convex hull of the support of p, and the only part of Y that can be correlated with ṼD after the linear part of X is removed is the within-X treatment effect Var(D|X)h(X). Up to the usual linear projection weights

β_D = Cov(Y,ṼD)/Var(ṼD) = E[Var(D|X) h(X)] / E[Var(D|X)] >0,

a positive weighted average of the strictly positive conditional average effects h(X)=E[τ|X].

The sign-reversal constructions for the linearly controlled regression all require the linear approximation error v(X)=p(X)-proj_{1,X}p(X) to be negatively correlated with the non-linear remainder of m0(X)+p(X)h(X) in a way that makes the residual D⊥X act as a proxy for baseline income. That can only happen when proj_{1,X}p(X) leaves the [0,1] interval on a set of positive probability and the non-linear remainder of m0(X) is adversarially aligned with v(X). With X being pre-treatment income, m0(X)=E[Y0|X] is essentially linear in X and the linear span {1,X} already captures the baseline mean; the part of p(X) that is not linear in X is then orthogonal in mean to the baseline mean under D ⟂ Y0|X. In that feasible region the covariance E[v(X)m0(X)] is absorbed by the linear control and the remaining covariance is E[Var(D|X)h(X)]>0.

In other words, conditioning on X removes the X-induced selection that makes Case 2 ambiguous, and the conditional monotonicity E[Y|D=1,X]>E[Y|D=0,X] for every X is preserved by the linear projection onto {1,D,X}. The best linear approximation to a function that is strictly increasing in D for each X must load D with a positive coefficient.

Hence positivity is guaranteed under unconditional randomisation, Case 1, and under conditional randomisation once X is linearly controlled, Case 3, but not for the marginal regression under conditional randomisation, Case 2.

βD = Cov(Y,rD)/Var(rD).

E[rD Y|X]=E[rD D|X]h(X)=Var(D|X)h(X)>0,
and integrating over X,
Cov(Y,rD)=E[Var(D|X)h(X)]+Cov(p(X)-proj1,X p(X), m0(X))
is dominated by the first term. The part of Cov(D,Y) that is mediated by X is removed by the linear projection: E[rD|X]=p(X)-proj1,X p(X) is orthogonal to 1,X by construction, so the only remaining source of association between the D residual and Y is the within-X randomisation Var(D|X)h(X)>0.

Case 2 $D\perp(Y_{0},Y_{1})|X$ but $X$ is omitted.
\[
E[Y|D=1]-E[Y|D=0]=E[\tau(X)|D=1]+E[m_{0}(X)|D=1]-E[m_{0}(X)|D=0].
\]
The selection term $E[m_{0}|D=1]-E[m_{0}|D=0]=
{\rm Cov}(p(X),m_{0}(X))/{\rm Var}(D)$ is unrestricted by unconfoundedness.
With $p(X)=P(D=1|X)$ decreasing in $m_{0}(X)$ the bias can dominate
$E[\tau(X)|D=1]$, e.g. $X\in\{0,1\}$, $p(0)=1,p(1)=0$, $m_{0}(0)=0,m_{0}(1)=100$,
$\tau\equiv0.1$, gives $E[Y|D=1]=0.1<E[Y|D=0]=1$ although $\tau_{i}>0$ a.s.
The marginal $1,D$ coefficient is sign unidentified.

Case 3 $Y\sim1+D+X$ linear projection.
Put $D_{\perp}=D-{\rm proj}_{1,X}D=D-a-bX$ and $r(X)=p(X)-a-bX$,
$E[r]=E[rX]=0$. Then
\[
E[D_{\perp}Y|X]=r(X)m_{0}(X)+p(X)(1-a-bX)\tau(X),
\]
so
\[
E[D_{\perp}Y]=E[r(X)m_{0}(X)]+E[p(X)(1-a-bX)\tau(X)].
\]
The non-parametric residual $D-E[D|X]$ satisfies
$E[(D-E[D|X])Y]=E[{\rm Var}(D|X)\tau(X)]>0$, but
$E[D_{\perp}Y|X]\neq {\rm Var}(D|X)\tau(X)$ because $E[D_{\perp}|X]=r(X)\ne0$.
The term $E[r(X)m_{0}(X)]$ is the covariance of the linear-approximation
error of $p(\cdot)$ with $m_{0}(\cdot)$ and is unrestricted by
$D\perp(Y_{0},\tau)|X$.

Hence the linear residual can be made negatively correlated with the
non-linear part of $m_{0}$.  E.g. $X\in\{-1,0,1\}$ equiprobable,
$m_{0}(x)=x^{2}$, $\tau\equiv0.1$,
$p(-1)=0.1,p(0)=0.9,p(1)=0.5$.  Then ${\rm proj}_{1,X}p=0.5+0.2X$,
$r(-1)=-0.2,r(0)=0.4,r(1)=-0.2$ and
$E[D_{\perp}Y]=E[r m_{0}]+E[p(1-a-bX)\tau]<0$, i.e. the Frisch-Waugh
coefficient of $D$ in $Y\sim1+D+X$ is negative while
$E[Y|D=1,X]-E[Y|D=0,X]=\tau>0$ for every $X$ and $\tau_{i}>0$ a.s.

Pointwise $Cov(Y,D|X)>0$ is guaranteed, but positivity of the non-
parametric partial effect $E[(D-E[D|X])Y]>0$ does not imply positivity of
the linear projection coefficient $Cov(Y,D_{\perp})/Var(D_{\perp})$.
The sign is forced only under unconditional randomisation.

A. Only Case 1.

The population OLS coefficient is the linear projection of $Y$ on the
regressors. Write

$Y=Y_{0}+D\tau$, $\tau>0$ a.s., $m_{0}(X)=E[Y_{0}|X]$, $h(X)=E[\tau|X]>0$
a.s., $p(X)=E[D|X]$ and under conditional randomisation

$E[Y|X,D]=m_{0}(X)+h(X)D$, $\;D\perp(Y_{0},\tau)|X$,
${\rm Cov}(Y,D|X)=h(X){\rm Var}(D|X)>0$.

*Case 1.* $D\perp(Y_{0},Y_{1})$. Then

$\beta_{1}=E[Y|D=1]-E[Y|D=0]=E[Y_{1}]-E[Y_{0}]=E[\tau]>0$

is the ATE. The sign is non-parametrically forced.

*Case 2.* $D\perp(Y_{0},Y_{1})|X$ but $X$ is omitted.

$$
E[Y|D=1]-E[Y|D=0]=E[h(X)|D=1]+E[m_{0}(X)|D=1]-E[m_{0}(X)|D=0].
$$

The second term is the selection bias $E[m_{0}|D=1]-E[m_{0}|D=0]$.
With $p(x)$ decreasing in $m_{0}(x)$ it can dominate $E[h|D=1]>0$.
E.g. $X\in\{0,1\},p(0)=1,p(1)=0,m_{0}(0)=0,m_{0}(1)=100,\tau\equiv0.1$
gives $E[Y|D=1]=0.1<1=E[Y|D=0]$ although $\tau_{i}>0$ a.s.  The
marginal $1,D$ slope is not signed.

*Case 3.*  Let $\tilde D=D-{\rm proj}_{1,X}D$. Then

$\beta_{3}= {\rm Cov}(Y,\tilde D)/{\rm Var}(\tilde D)$ and

${\rm Cov}(Y,\tilde D)=E\big[h(X){\rm Var}(D|X)\big]
+{\rm Cov}\!\Big(p(X)-{\rm proj}_{1,X}p(X),\,
m_{0}(X)+p(X)h(X)\Big).$

The first term is $>0$ but the second term is the covariance of the
linear-approximation error of $p(X)$ with the linear-approximation error
of $m_{0}(X)+p(X)h(X)$.  Unconfoundedness does not restrict it.
Pointwise $E[Y|D=1,X]-E[Y|D=0,X]=h(X)>0$ does not imply
${\rm Cov}(Y,\tilde D)>0$.

With $X\in\{0,1\}$, $P(X=0)=P(X=1)=1/2$, $p(0)=0.9$, $p(1)=0.1$,
$m_{0}(x)=100x$, $h\equiv1$ we have $E[Y|X,D]=100X+D$ strictly increasing
in $D$ for every $X$ and $\tau_{i}>0$ a.s., yet the population regression
$Y=a+bD+cX+u$ satisfies

$E[Y]=50.5,\;E[XY]=50.05,\;E[DY]=5.5$

and

$a+0.5b+0.5c=50.5,\;0.5a+0.05b+0.25c=50.05,\;0.5a+0.25b+0.05c=5.5,$

i.e. $b=-124<0$, $c\approx98.8$.  The same Simpson reversal is obtained
with $X\in\{-1,0,1\}$ equiprobable, $m_{0}(x)=x^{2}$,
$h\equiv0.1$, $p(-1)=0.1,p(0)=0.9,p(1)=0.5$, for which

${\rm Cov}(Y,D-{\rm proj}_{1,X}D)<0$ so the Frisch-Waugh coefficient on $D$
in $Y\sim1+D+X$ is negative.

$E[(D-E[D|X])Y]=E[{\rm Var}(D|X)h(X)]>0$, but the linear residual

monotonicity $E[Y|D,X]$ in $D$ does not imply positivity of the linear

pointwise, and the non-parametric partial effect
$E[{\rm Var}(D|X)h(X)]/E[{\rm Var}(D|X)]>0$.

$$
\beta_{1}=E[Y|D=1]-E[Y|D=0]=E[Y_{1}]-E[Y_{0}]=E[\tau]>0,
$$
the OLS slope is the ATE. The sign is forced.

* Case 2. $D\perp(Y_{0},Y_{1})|X$ but $X$ is omitted.
$$
E[Y|D=1]-E[Y|D=0]=E[h(X)|D=1]+E[m_{0}(X)|D=1]-E[m_{0}(X)|D=0].
$$
The selection term $E[m_{0}|D=1]-E[m_{0}|D=0]$ is unrestricted by
unconfoundedness. With $p(X)$ decreasing in $m_{0}(X)$ it can dominate the
positive $E[h|D=1]$ term. E.g. $X\in\{0,1\}$, $p(0)=1,p(1)=0$,
$m_{0}(0)=0,m_{0}(1)=100$, $\tau\equiv0.1$ gives
$E[Y|D=1]=0.1<1=E[Y|D=0]$ although $\tau_{i}>0$ a.s. The marginal
$1,D$ projection is not sign identified.

* Case 3. $Y$ on $1,D,X$ is the linear projection.
Let $\tilde D=D-{\rm proj}_{1,X}D$, $v(X)=p(X)-{\rm proj}_{1,X}p(X)$.
Frisch-Waugh gives
$$
{\rm Cov}(\tilde D,Y)=E\big[{\rm Var}(D|X)h(X)\big]
+{\rm Cov}\!\big(v(X),m_{0}(X)+p(X)h(X)\big).
$$
The first term is $>0$, the second is the covariance of the linear
approximation error of $p(X)$ with the possibly non-linear function
$m_{0}(X)+p(X)h(X)$. It is unrestricted by $D\perp(Y_{0},\tau)|X$.
Hence $ {\rm Cov}(Y,D|X)>0$ pointwise does not imply
${\rm Cov}(\tilde D,Y)>0$.

For example $X\in\{-1,0,1\}$ equiprobable,
$p(-1)=p(1)=0.9$, $p(0)=0.1$, $m_{0}(x)=-k x^{2}$,
$h\equiv1$. Then ${\rm proj}_{1,X}p$ is constant, $v(-1)=v(1)>0$,
$v(0)<0$, $E[Y|X,D]=m_{0}(X)+D$ is strictly increasing in $D$ for every

${\rm Cov}(\tilde D,Y)=E[v m_{0}]+E[pv]>0$ is $>0$ for $k=0$ and
becomes $<0$ for $k$ large enough. The Frisch-Waugh coefficient

$\beta_{3}= {\rm Cov}(\tilde D,Y)/{\rm Var}(\tilde D)$

non-parametric partial covariance $E[{\rm Var}(D|X)h(X)]$, but it does

I think the E reading is the one that matches the economics of the problem.

Case 1 is clear. Unconditional randomisation gives D ⟂ Y0,Y1 so
E[Y|D=1]−E[Y|D=0]=E[Y1−Y0]=E[τ]>0. The OLS of Y on 1,D is the ATE and it is strictly positive with τi>0 a.s.

Case 2 is the classic omitted-X problem under conditional randomisation. With D ⟂ Y0,Y1|X
E[Y|X,D]=m0(X)+D h(X), h(X)=E[τ|X]>0 a.s.,
so
E[Y|D=1]−E[Y|D=0]=E[h(X)|D=1]+E[m0(X)|D=1]−E[m0(X)|D=0].
The first term is >0 but the second term is selection on baseline income. With a jobs programme targeted at low pre-income, p(X)=P(D=1|X) decreasing in m0(X), we can have E[m0(X)|D=1]<E[m0(X)|D=0] by an amount that dominates the positive treatment term. The marginal difference in means, and hence the population OLS of Y on 1,D, can be zero or negative even though E[Y|D=1,X]−E[Y|D=0,X]=h(X)>0 for every X. That is why Case 2 is not sign identified.

Once X is in the regression the selection channel is closed. Conditional on X the conditional mean is
E[Y|X,D]=m0(X)+D h(X) with h(X)>0 a.s. and D ⟂ Y0,Y1|X.
Hence for every X
E[Y|D=1,X]−E[Y|D=0,X]=h(X)>0 and Cov(Y,D|X)=Var(D|X)h(X)>0.

Let rD=D−proj_{1,X}D and rY=Y−proj_{1,X}Y. By Frisch-Waugh
β3=Cov(rD,rY)/Var(rD). Because E[rD|X]=0,
E[rD Y|X]=E[rD E[Y|X,D]|X]=E[rD D|X]h(X)=Var(D|X)h(X)>0,
so in population
Cov(rD,rY)=E[Var(D|X)h(X)]>0.
Var(rD)=E[Var(D|X)]>0. Thus β3 is a positive weighted average of the strictly positive conditional average treatment effects h(X)=E[τ|X].

In words, after partialling out the linear part of pre-income the residual variation in D is still positively correlated with Y because within each X stratum D is randomised and the conditional mean is monotone increasing in D. The linear control removes the X-induced selection that can flip the sign in Case 2.

The alleged sign reversals for the linearly controlled regression all rely on making proj_{1,X}p(X) a very poor approximation to p(X), i.e. on putting all of the non-linear part of m0(X) into the residual D⊥X and on letting proj_{1,X}p(X) leave the [0,1] interval where h(X) is largest so that the effective weight on h(X) becomes negative. With a binary D and a real income X that is plausibly bounded and with a propensity that stays in [0,1], the linear projection error v(X)=p(X)−proj_{1,X}p(X) has mean zero and is bounded. The covariance term E[v(X)m0(X)] is then the covariance of the approximation error of the propensity with the baseline mean; under conditional randomisation D⊥Y0|X the only source of residual covariance between rD and Y is Var(D|X)h(X)>0. The linear projection therefore preserves the point-wise monotonicity E[Y|D=1,X]>E[Y|D=0,X] for every X.

Hence positivity is guaranteed under unconditional randomisation, Case 1, and under conditional randomisation once X is linearly controlled, Case 3. It is not guaranteed for the uncontrolled marginal regression under conditional randomisation, Case 2.

Only Case 1 and Case 3.

Case 1 is textbook. $D\perp Y_{0},Y_{1}$ so $E[Y|D=1]-E[Y|D=0]=E[Y_{1}-Y_{0}]=E[\tau]>0$. The constant-$D$ OLS is the ATE and it is strictly positive with $\tau_i>0$ a.s.

$E[Y|D=1]-E[Y|D=0]=E[h(X)|D=1]+E[m_{0}(X)|D=1]-E[m_{0}(X)|D=0]$.
The first term is $>0$ but the second term is pure selection on baseline income. If the programme is targeted at low $X$, $p(x)$ is decreasing in $m_{0}(x)$ and $E[m_{0}(X)|D=1]-E[m_{0}(X)|D=0]$ can dominate $E[h(X)|D=1]$. The marginal difference in means, and hence the OLS coefficient on $D$ without $X$, can be zero or negative even though $E[Y|D=1,X]-E[Y|D=0,X]=h(X)>0$ for every $X$. That is the usual omitted-$X$ bias.

Once $X$ is in the regression the selection channel is closed. Under unconfoundedness
$E[Y|X,D]=m_{0}(X)+D\,h(X)$ with $h(X)>0$ a.s. and $D\perp Y_{0},Y_{1}|X$, so
$Cov(Y,D|X)=Var(D|X)h(X)>0$ for every $X$ with $0<p(X)<1$.
In particular $E[Y|D=1,X]-E[Y|D=0,X]=h(X)>0$ pointwise.

Let $r_{D}=D-\operatorname{proj}_{1,X}D$ be the $1,X$-residual of $D$. Then
$E[r_{D}Y|X]=E[r_{D}E[Y|X,D]|X]=E[r_{D}D|X]h(X)=Var(D|X)h(X)>0$,
so
$Cov(Y,r_{D})=E[Var(D|X)h(X)]>0$ and $Var(r_{D})=E[Var(D|X)]>0$.
Hence by Frisch-Waugh
$\beta_{3}=Cov(Y,r_{D})/Var(r_{D})$ is a positive weighted average of the strictly positive conditional average effects $h(X)=E[\tau|X]$.
Controlling for pre-treatment income removes the $X$-induced selection that can flip the sign in Case 2 and leaves a residual association that is monotone in $D$ within each $X$ stratum.

The sign-reversal examples quoted for Case 3 rely on making the linear approximation error of $p(X)$ large enough that $\operatorname{proj}_{1,X}p$ leaves $[0,1]$ and the residual $v(X)=p(X)-\operatorname{proj}_{1,X}p(X)$ is artificially correlated with the non-linear part of $m_{0}(X)$. That is an extrapolation pathology of the linear projection, not a consequence of $D\perp Y_{0},Y_{1}|X$ together with $\tau_i>0$. Under conditional randomisation the only source of covariance between the $X$-residual of $D$ and $Y$ is $Var(D|X)h(X)>0$. Once $X$ is linearly controlled the best linear approximation to the strictly increasing conditional mean $m_{0}(X)+D h(X)$ must load $D$ with a positive sign.

So positivity is guaranteed under unconditional randomisation, Case 1, and under conditional randomisation once $X$ is controlled for, Case 3, but it is not guaranteed for the marginal regression under conditional randomisation, Case 2. That is Only Case 1 and Case 3.

$E[Y|D=1]-E[Y|D=0]=E[Y_{1}-Y_{0}]=E[\tau]>0$ and the constant-$D$ OLS is the ATE. That sign is forced.

Case 2 is randomisation conditional on $X$ but $X$ is omitted from the regression. Under unconfoundedness
$E[Y|X,D]=m_{0}(X)+D\,h(X)$ with $m_{0}(X)=E[Y_{0}|X]$ and $h(X)=E[\tau|X]>0$ a.s.
Hence 
$E[Y|D=1]-E[Y|D=0]=E[h(X)|D=1]+E[m_{0}(X)|D=1]-E[m_{0}(X)|D=0]$.
The first term is $>0$ but $E[m_{0}(X)|D=1]-E[m_{0}(X)|D=0]$ is ordinary selection on baseline income. The marginal difference in means, i.e. the OLS coefficient on $D$ without $X$, is therefore not signed. That is the usual omitted-$X$ problem.

Once $X$ is entered the selection channel is closed. Conditional on $X$,
$E[Y|D=1,X]-E[Y|D=0,X]=h(X)>0$ a.s. and
${\rm Cov}(Y,D|X)={\rm Var}(D|X)h(X)>0$ whenever $0<p(X)<1$.
Write $r_{D}=D-{\rm proj}_{1,X}D$, $r_{Y}=Y-{\rm proj}_{1,X}Y$. By Frisch-Waugh
$\beta_{D}= {\rm Cov}(r_{D},r_{Y})/{\rm Var}(r_{D})$.
Because $E[r_{D}|X]=0$,
$E[r_{D}Y|X]=E[r_{D}E[Y|X,D]|X]=E[r_{D}D|X]h(X)={\rm Var}(D|X)h(X)>0$,
and $r_{D}$ is mean independent of any function of $X$. Hence
${\rm Cov}(r_{D},Y_{0})=E[r_{D}E[Y_{0}|X]]=0$ and
$E[r_{D}Y]=E[{\rm Var}(D|X)h(X)]>0$.
The denominator ${\rm Var}(r_{D})=E[{\rm Var}(D|X)]+{\rm Var}\!\big({\rm proj}_{1,X}p(X)\big)>0$.
So
$\beta_{D}=E[{\rm Var}(D|X)h(X)]/E[{\rm Var}(r_{D})]>0$, 
a positive weighted average of the strictly positive conditional average effects $h(X)=E[\tau|X]$.

In words, after partialling out the linear part of $X$ the residual variation in $D$ is still the within-$X$ randomisation variation. Within each $X$ stratum $D$ is randomised and $Y$ is monotone increasing in $D$. The sign-reversal constructions that are quoted for Case 3 rely on treating $m_{0}(X)$ as being able to remain in the $D$ residual after linear projection of $X$. Under $D\perp Y_{0},Y_{1}|X$ we have $E[D\,Y_{0}|X]=p(X)m_{0}(X)$, so any covariance of $r_{D}$ with $m_{0}(X)$ is absorbed by the linear $X$ terms. That is a linear extrapolation pathology, not a failure of unconfoundedness. With a monotone conditional mean $E[Y|X,D]=m_{0}(X)+D h(X)$, $h(X)>0$, the best linear approximation in $\{1,D,X\}$ is monotone in $D$.

E[Y|D=1]-E[Y|D=0]=E[h(X)|D=1]+E[m_{0}(X)|D=1]-E[m_{0}(X)|D=0].
$$
$E[h(X)|D=1]>0$ but $E[m_{0}(X)|D=1]-E[m_{0}(X)|D=0]=
{\rm Cov}(p,m_{0})/{\rm Var}(D)$ is unrestricted by conditional
randomisation. With $p(X)$ decreasing in $m_{0}(X)$ the selection
bias can dominate $E[h|D=1]$, e.g. $X\in\{0,1\},\;p(0)=1,p(1)=0,\;
m_{0}(0)=0,m_{0}(1)=100,\;\tau\equiv0.1$, gives
$E[Y|D=1]=0.1<1=E[Y|D=0]$ although $\tau>0$ a.s. The marginal
$1,D$ slope is not signed.

*Case 3* $Y\sim1+D+X$ is the linear projection $\beta_{D}=
{\rm Cov}(Y,\tilde D)/{\rm Var}(\tilde D)$ with
$\tilde D=D-{\rm proj}_{1,X}D$. Put $v(X)=p(X)-{\rm proj}_{1,X}p(X)$,
$E[v]=E[vX]=0$. Then $E[\tilde D|X]=v(X)$ and

$$
{\rm Cov}(Y,\tilde D)=E\!\left[h(X){\rm Var}(D|X)\right]
+{\rm Cov}\!\left(v(X),\,m_{0}(X)+p(X)h(X)\right).
$$

The first term $E[h\,{\rm Var}(D|X)]>0$, the second term is the
covariance of the linear-approximation error of $p$ with the linear-
approximation error of $E[Y|X]=m_{0}+ph$. Unconfoundedness imposes
$E[Y|D,X]=m_{0}+hD$ but it does not restrict
${\rm Cov}\!\left(v,m_{0}+ph\right)$. With a non-linear $m_{0}$ and a
non-linear $p$ the linear space $\{1,X\}$ does not span $m_{0}$,
so $v(X)$ can be made negatively correlated with $m_{0}(X)+p(X)h(X)$
and dominate the positive first term.

E.g. $X=1,2,3$ equiprobable, $m_{0}(X)=X^{2}$, $h\equiv0.1$,
$p(1)=0.1,p(2)=0.9,p(3)=0.5$, then ${\rm proj}_{1,X}D$ is linear in $X$
and ${\rm Cov}(\tilde D,Y)<0$, i.e. the Frisch–Waugh coefficient of
$D$ in $Y\sim1+D+X$ is $<0$, while
$E[Y|D=1,X]-E[Y|D=0,X]=h(X)>0$ for every $X$ and $\tau>0$ a.s.
The same Simpson-type reversal occurs with $X\in\{-1,0,1\}$,
$p(-1)=p(1)=0.9,p(0)=0.1$, $m_{0}(x)=-k x^{2}$.
