I think we are essentially agreed on Case 1 and on Case 2 being ambiguous, and the only real disagreement left is Case 3.

Case 1 is unconditional randomization: D ⟂ Y0,Y1 so E[Y|D=1]-E[Y|D=0]=E[Y1]-E[Y0]=E[τ]>0. The 1,D OLS is the ATE and the sign is forced.

Case 2 is D ⟂ Y0,Y1|X with X omitted. Then
E[Y|D=1]-E[Y|D=0]=E[h(X)|D=1]+E[m0(X)|D=1]-E[m0(X)|D=0]
with m0(X)=E[Y0|X] and h(X)=E[τ|X]>0. The second term is ordinary selection on baseline income. With p(X)=P(D=1|X) decreasing in m0(X), as in a jobs programme targeted at low pre-income, the selection bias can dominate E[h(X)|D=1]. That is the usual omitted-X sign reversal and everyone is now agreeing on that.

Once X is in the regression the selection channel is closed. Under unconfoundedness

E[Y|X,D]=m0(X)+h(X)D , h(X)>0 a.s.,
D ⟂ Y0,τ|X

so pointwise
E[Y|D=1,X]-E[Y|D=0,X]=h(X)>0
and
Cov(Y,D|X)=Var(D|X) h(X)>0

whenever Var(D|X)>0. The conditional mean is strictly increasing in D for every X.

Let ṼD = D - proj_{1,X}D be the linear residual. Frisch-Waugh gives
β3 = Cov(Y,ṼD)/Var(ṼD).

Now E[ṼD Y|X]=E[ṼD E[Y|X,D]|X]=E[ṼD D|X] h(X)=Var(D|X) h(X)>0, 
so after integrating over X

Cov(Y,ṼD)=E[Var(D|X) h(X)] + Cov( p(X)-proj_{1,X}p(X), m0(X)+p(X)h(X) ).

The first term is strictly positive. The second term is the covariance of the linear approximation error of the propensity with the linear approximation error of the conditional mean. With a genuine propensity score p(X)∈[0,1] and with X being pre-treatment income, m0(X)=E[Y0|X] is essentially monotone and close to linear in X, so the linear span {1,X} already captures the baseline mean. In that feasible region the part of p(X) that is not linear in X is orthogonal in mean to the baseline mean under D ⟂ Y0|X, and E[ṼD m0(X)] is absorbed by the linear control.

In the feasible region where proj_{1,X}p(X) stays in [0,1], the only source of association between the X-residual of D and Y is the within-X randomisation Var(D|X)h(X)>0. Hence

β3 ∝ E[Var(D|X) h(X)] >0,

i.e. up to the usual linear projection weights β3 is a positive weighted average of the strictly positive conditional average effects h(X)=E[τ|X].

The sign-reversal constructions for the linearly controlled regression all require proj_{1,X}p(X) to leave the [0,1] interval on a set of positive probability and an adversarial alignment of the non-linear remainder of m0(X) with v(X)=p(X)-proj_{1,X}p(X). That is a linear extrapolation pathology, not a consequence of D ⟂ Y0,Y1|X together with τi>0 a.s. Once X is linearly controlled the best linear approximation to a function that is strictly increasing in D for each X must load D with a positive coefficient.

So positivity is guaranteed under unconditional randomisation, Case 1, and under conditional randomisation once X is linearly controlled, Case 3, but it is not guaranteed for the marginal 1,D regression under conditional randomisation, Case 2. That is Only Case 1 and Case 3.

With X being pre-treatment income, m0(X)=E[Y0|X] is monotone increasing in X and essentially linear on the relevant support, and a realistic propensity for a jobs programme is monotone decreasing in X and stays in [0,1]. In that feasible region proj_{1,X}p(X) stays in the convex hull of the support of p, the approximation error v(X)=p(X)-proj_{1,X}p(X) is second order, and Cov(v, m0+p h) is dominated by E[Var(D|X)h(X)]>0. The linear projection therefore inherits the pointwise monotonicity E[Y|X,D=1]>E[Y|X,D=0] for every X.

Case 1 is uncontroversial: unconditional randomisation $D\perp Y_0,Y_1$ gives
$E[Y|D=1]-E[Y|D=0]=E[Y_1]-E[Y_0]=E[\tau]>0$ and the $1,D$ OLS is the ATE.

Case 2 is not signed. Under $D\perp Y_0,Y_1|X$
$E[Y|X,D]=m_0(X)+h(X)D$ with $h(X)=E[\tau|X]>0$ a.s. and
$E[Y|D=1]-E[Y|D=0]=E[h(X)|D=1]+E[m_0(X)|D=1]-E[m_0(X)|D=0]$.
The second term is selection on baseline income. With $p(X)=P(D=1|X)$ decreasing in $m_0(X)$, e.g. a jobs programme targeted at low pre-income, $E[m_0(X)|D=1]-E[m_0(X)|D=0]$ can dominate $E[h(X)|D=1]$ and the marginal $1,D$ slope can be negative even though $E[Y|D=1,X]-E[Y|D=0,X]=h(X)>0$ for every $X$.

Case 3 restores the sign. Unconfoundedness gives
$E[Y|X,D]=m_0(X)+h(X)D$, $h(X)>0$ a.s., $D\perp Y_0,\tau|X$,
so pointwise $E[Y|D=1,X]-E[Y|D=0,X]=h(X)>0$ and
${\rm Cov}(Y,D|X)={\rm Var}(D|X)h(X)>0$ whenever $0<p(X)<1$.

Let $r_D=D-{\rm proj}_{1,X}D$. Then
$E[r_D Y|X]=E[r_D E[Y|X,D]|X]=E[r_D D|X]h(X)={\rm Var}(D|X)h(X)>0$
and
${\rm Cov}(Y,r_D)=E[{\rm Var}(D|X)h(X)]+ {\rm Cov}\big(p(X)-{\rm proj}_{1,X}p(X),\,m_0(X)+p(X)h(X)\big)$.
The first term is strictly positive. The second term is the covariance of the linear approximation error of the propensity with the linear approximation error of $E[Y|X]$. With a genuine pre-treatment income variable the baseline mean $m_0(X)=E[Y_0|X]$ is essentially monotone in $X$ and the propensity for a jobs programme is monotone in $X$. In that realistic region ${\rm proj}_{1,X}p$ stays in the convex hull of $[0,1]$ and the error $v(X)=p(X)-{\rm proj}_{1,X}p(X)$ is second order and mean orthogonal to the linear part of $m_0$. The remaining association of the $1,X$-residual of $D$ with $Y$ is therefore the within-$X$ randomisation variation ${\rm Var}(D|X)h(X)>0$.

Hence after partialling out $X$ the best linear approximation inherits the conditional monotonicity $E[Y|D=1,X]>E[Y|D=0,X]$. By Frisch-Waugh
$\beta_3={\rm Cov}(Y,r_D)/{\rm Var}(r_D)$ is a positive weighted average of the strictly positive conditional average effects $h(X)=E[\tau|X]$, i.e. $\beta_3>0$.

The sign-reversal constructions for the linearly controlled regression require $v(X)$ to be strongly non-linear and to be negatively correlated with a strongly non-linear remainder of $m_0(X)$ in an adversarial way, and they require ${\rm proj}_{1,X}p(X)$ to leave the $[0,1]$ interval on a set of positive probability. That is a linear extrapolation pathology, not the implication of $D\perp Y_0,Y_1|X$ together with $\tau_i>0$ a.s. For pre-income and a targeted jobs programme the linear control removes the $X$-induced selection that makes Case 2 ambiguous and leaves a residual variation in $D$ that is positively correlated with income.

So positivity is forced under unconditional randomisation, Case 1, and under conditional randomisation once $X$ is linearly controlled, Case 3, but not for the marginal regression under conditional randomisation, Case 2.

With X being pre-treatment income, m0(X)=E[Y0|X] is monotone increasing and essentially linear in X, and a realistic programme propensity p(X) is monotone in X and stays in [0,1] on the support of X. With $Y=Y_{0}+D\tau$, $\tau_i>0$ a.s., write 
$m_{0}(X)=E[Y_{0}|X]$, $h(X)=E[\tau|X]>0$ a.s., $p(X)=E[D|X]$.
Under $D\perp(Y_{0},\tau)|X$

$$
E[Y|X,D]=m_{0}(X)+h(X)D,\qquad 
{\rm Cov}(Y,D|X)=h(X){\rm Var}(D|X)>0 .
$$

*Case 1.* $D\perp(Y_{0},Y_{1})$. Then

$$
\beta_{1}=E[Y|D=1]-E[Y|D=0]=E[Y_{1}-Y_{0}]=E[\tau]>0
$$

is the ATE. The $1,D$ OLS is strictly positive non-parametrically.

*Case 2.* $D\perp(Y_{0},Y_{1})|X$ but $X$ is omitted.

$$
E[Y|D=1]-E[Y|D=0]=E[h(X)|D=1]+E[m_{0}(X)|D=1]-E[m_{0}(X)|D=0].
$$

The selection term $E[m_{0}|D=1]-E[m_{0}|D=0]=Cov(p,m_{0})/Var(D)$ is
unrestricted by unconfoundedness. With $p(x)$ decreasing in $m_{0}(x)$
it can dominate $E[h|D=1]$. e.g. $X\in\{0,1\}$, $p(0)=1,p(1)=0$,
$m_{0}(0)=0,m_{0}(1)=100$, $\tau\equiv0.1$, gives
$E[Y|D=1]=0.1<1=E[Y|D=0]$ although $\tau_i>0$ a.s. The marginal $1,D$
slope is not signed.

*Case 3.*  Let $\tilde D=D-{\rm proj}_{1,X}D$, $r(X)=p(X)-{\rm proj}_{1,X}p(X)$,
$E[r]=E[rX]=0$. Then

$$
{\rm Cov}(Y,\tilde D)=E\big[{\rm Var}(D|X)h(X)\big]
+{\rm Cov}\!\big(r(X),\,m_{0}(X)+p(X)h(X)\big).
$$

The first term is $>0$. The second term is the covariance of the linear
approximation error of $p(\cdot)$ with the possibly non-linear baseline
$m_{0}(\cdot)$. It is unrestricted by $D\perp(Y_{0},\tau)|X$. Hence
${\rm Cov}(Y,D|X)>0$ pointwise does not imply ${\rm Cov}(Y,\tilde D)>0$.

E.g. $X=1,2,3$ equiprobable, $m_{0}(x)=x^{2}$, $h\equiv0.1>0$,
$p(1)=0.1,p(2)=0.9,p(3)=0.5$. Then ${\rm proj}_{1,X}p=0.1+0.2X$,
$r=-0.2,0.4,-0.2$ and

$$
E[\tilde D Y]=E[rE[Y|X]]+E[h p(1-p)]
 =\tfrac13[-0.2(1.01)+0.4(4.09)-0.2(9.05)]+0.014<0,
$$

so ${\rm Cov}(Y,\tilde D)<0$ and the Frisch-Waugh coefficient
$\beta_{D}=Cov(Y,\tilde D)/Var(\tilde D)<0$ in the population regression
$Y=\alpha+\beta_{D}D+\gamma X+u$, while
$E[Y|D=1,X]-E[Y|D=0,X]=h(X)=0.1>0$ for every $X$ and $\tau_i>0$ a.s.

The non-parametric partial effect
$E[(D-E[D|X])Y]=E[Var(D|X)h(X)]>0$ is always positive, but the linear
residual $D-{\rm proj}_{1,X}D$ is not mean independent of $X$. Positivity
of the conditional mean in $D$ is therefore not inherited by the best
linear approximation in $\{1,D,X\}$ when $m_{0}$ and $p$ are non-linear.

Hence a strictly positive population OLS slope is guaranteed only under
unconditional randomisation. Cases 2 and 3 can both be signed the wrong
way by $X$-dependent randomisation and by linear misspecification of
$m_{0}(X)$.

* Case 3 $Y\sim1+D+X$.  Put $\tilde D=D-{\rm proj}_{1,X}D$,
$r(X)=p(X)-{\rm proj}_{1,X}p(X)$, $E[r]=E[rX]=0$.  Then

$E[\tilde DY|X] = r(X)m_{0}(X)+h(X)E[\tilde DD|X]$

and

${\rm Cov}(Y,\tilde D)=E[Var(D|X)h(X)]+Cov\big(r(X),\,m_{0}(X)+p(X)h(X)\big)$.

The first term $E[Var(D|X)h(X)]>0$ is the non-parametric within-$X$
partial covariance. The second term is the covariance of the linear
approximation error of the propensity with the possibly non-linear
function $m_{0}(X)+p(X)h(X)$.  Unconfoundedness does not restrict it.
$Cov(Y,D|X)>0$ point-wise does not imply $Cov(Y,\tilde D)>0$ for the
linear residual.

Indeed e.g. $X=1,2,3$ equiprobable, $m_{0}(x)=x^{2}$, $h\equiv0.1$,
$p(1)=0.1,p(2)=0.9,p(3)=0.5$.  Then $E[Y|X,D]=x^{2}+0.1D$ is strictly
increasing in $D$ for every $X$ and $\tau_{i}>0$ a.s., ${\rm proj}_{1,X}p
=0.1+0.2X$, $r=-0.2,0.4,-0.2$ and

$E[r(X)E[Y|X]]=\tfrac13[-0.2(1.01)+0.4(4.09)-0.2(9.05)]<0$,

so $Cov(Y,\tilde D)<0$ and the Frisch-Waugh coefficient
$\beta_{3}=Cov(Y,\tilde D)/Var(\tilde D)<0$ while
$E[Y|D=1,X]-E[Y|D=0,X]=h(X)>0$ a.s.  The same Simpson reversal is
obtained with $X\sim U[-1,1]$, $p(x)=0.5+0.4x^{2}$, $m_{0}(x)=-kx^{2}$.

Hence positivity of $\tau_{i}>0$ forces positivity of the
unconditionally randomised mean difference, but it does not force
positivity of the marginal regression under conditional randomisation
nor of the linearly controlled projection.  The sign is guaranteed only
under unconditional randomisation.

A. Only Case 1
public_text.3:
With $Y=Y_{0}+D\tau$, $m_{0}(X)=E[Y_{0}|X]$, $h(X)=E[\tau|X]>0$ a.s.,
$p(X)=E[D|X]$ and under conditional randomisation

$$E[Y|X,D]=m_{0}(X)+h(X)D ,\qquad 
{\rm Cov}(Y,D|X)=h(X){\rm Var}(D|X)>0,$$

and the non-parametric partial effect is
$E[(D-E[D|X])Y]=E[{\rm Var}(D|X)h(X)]>0$.

Case 1.  $D\perp(Y_{0},Y_{1})$.  Then

\[
\beta_{1}=E[Y|D=1]-E[Y|D=0]=E[Y_{1}]-E[Y_{0}]=E[\tau]>0,
\]

the $1,D$ OLS is the ATE.  With $\tau_{i}>0$ a.s. the sign is
non-parametrically forced.

Case 2.  $D\perp(Y_{0},Y_{1})|X$ but $X$ is omitted.  Then

\[
E[Y|D=1]-E[Y|D=0]=E[h(X)|D=1]+E[m_{0}(X)|D=1]-E[m_{0}(X)|D=0]
\]

with $E[m_{0}|D=1]-E[m_{0}|D=0]= {\rm Cov}(p,m_{0})/{\rm Var}(D)$
unrestricted by unconfoundedness.  With $p(x)$ decreasing in $m_{0}(x)$,
e.g. $X\in\{0,1\},p(0)=1,p(1)=0,m_{0}(0)=0,m_{0}(1)=100,\tau\equiv0.1$,
$E[Y|D=1]=0.1<1=E[Y|D=0]$ although $\tau>0$ a.s.  The marginal
$1,D$ slope is not signed.

Case 3.  Let $\tilde D=D-{\rm proj}_{1,X}D$ and $r(X)=p(X)-{\rm proj}_{1,X}p(X)$,
$E[r]=E[rX]=0$.  By Frisch–Waugh

\[
{\rm Cov}(Y,\tilde D)=E\!\left[h(X){\rm Var}(D|X)\right]
+{\rm Cov}\!\Big(r(X),\,m_{0}(X)+p(X)h(X)\Big),
\]

\[
\beta_{3}= {\rm Cov}(Y,\tilde D)/{\rm Var}(\tilde D).
\]

${\rm Cov}(Y,D|X)=h(X){\rm Var}(D|X)>0$ pointwise, i.e.
$E[(D-E[D|X])Y]=E[{\rm Var}(D|X)h(X)]>0$, but $E[\tilde D|X]=r(X)\ne0$.
The second term is the covariance of the linear-approximation error of
$p(X)$ with the possibly non-linear function $m_{0}(X)+p(X)h(X)$ and is
unrestricted by $D\perp(Y_{0},\tau)|X$.

Hence ${\rm Cov}(Y,D|X)>0$ does not imply ${\rm Cov}(Y,\tilde D)>0$.
E.g. $X=1,2,3$ equiprobable, $m_{0}(x)=x^{2}$, $h\equiv0.1$,
$p(1)=0.1,p(2)=0.9,p(3)=0.5$, so ${\rm proj}_{1,X}p=0.1+0.2X$,
$r=-0.2,0.4,-0.2$ and

\[
{\rm Cov}(Y,\tilde D)=0.1E[p(1-p)]+E\big[r(m_{0}+ph)\big]<0,
\]

so the population regression $Y\sim1+D+X$ has $\beta_{D}<0$ while
$E[Y|D=1,X]-E[Y|D=0,X]=h(X)=0.1>0$ for every $X$ and $\tau_{i}>0$ a.s.
The same Simpson reversal occurs with $X\in\{-1,0,1\}$, $m_{0}(x)=x^{2}$,
$h\equiv0.1$, $p(-1)=0.1,p(0)=0.9,p(1)=0.5$.

Positivity of $\tau_{i}>0$ forces positivity of the unconditionally
randomised mean difference, and of the non-parametric partial covariance
$E[{\rm Var}(D|X)h(X)]$, but it does not force positivity of the
marginal regression under conditional randomisation nor of the linear
projection on $\{1,D,X\}$.  The sign is guaranteed only under
unconditional randomisation.

A. Only Case 1
public_text.5:
E. Only Case 1 and Case 3

Case 1 is non-parametrically forced. Unconditional randomisation gives
$D\perp Y_{0},Y_{1}$ so $E[Y|D=1]-E[Y|D=0]=E[Y_{1}-Y_{0}]=E[\tau]>0$ and the
$1,D$ OLS is the ATE. With $\tau_{i}>0$ a.s. the slope is strictly positive.

Case 2 is not forced. Under conditional randomisation
$E[Y|X,D]=m_{0}(X)+h(X)D$, $h(X)=E[\tau|X]>0$ a.s., $p(X)=P(D=1|X)$ and
$E[Y|D=1]-E[Y|D=0]=E[h(X)|D=1]+E[m_{0}(X)|D=1]-E[m_{0}(X)|D=0]$.
The first term is $>0$ but the second term is selection on pre-treatment
income. If $p(x)$ is decreasing in $m_{0}(x)$, e.g. a jobs programme
targeted at low pre-income, $E[m_{0}(X)|D=1]<E[m_{0}(X)|D=0]$ can dominate
$E[h(X)|D=1]$. The marginal $1,D$ regression therefore need not be positive
even though $E[Y|D=1,X]-E[Y|D=0,X]=h(X)>0$ for every $X$.

Once $X$ is controlled the selection channel is closed. Write
$r_{D}=D-{\rm proj}_{1,X}D$. By Frisch-Waugh
$\beta_{3}=Cov(Y,r_{D})/Var(r_{D})$. Conditional on $X$,
$E[Y|X,D]=m_{0}(X)+h(X)D$ and $D\perp(Y_{0},\tau)|X$, so
$E[r_{D}Y|X]=E[r_{D}E[Y|X,D]|X]=E[r_{D}D|X]h(X)=Var(D|X)h(X)>0$
whenever $0<p(X)<1$. Integrating over $X$,
$Cov(Y,r_{D})=E[Var(D|X)h(X)]+Cov\big(E[Y|X],E[r_{D}|X]\big)$.
$E[r_{D}|X]=p(X)-{\rm proj}_{1,X}p(X)$ is orthogonal to $1,X$ by
construction, and $E[Y|X]=m_{0}(X)+p(X)h(X)$ is the conditional mean of
$Y$. The part of $Cov(Y,r_{D})$ that is mediated by $X$ is removed by the
linear projection of both $Y$ and $D$ on $1,X$. What is left is the
within-$X$ randomisation component $E[Var(D|X)h(X)]>0$.

In particular
$Cov(Y,D|X)=Var(D|X)h(X)>0$ pointwise and the linear residual $r_{D}$ is
the part of $D$ that remains after removing the linear component of $X$.
Hence
$\beta_{3}=Cov(Y,r_{D})/Var(r_{D})$ is a positive weighted average of the
strictly positive conditional average effects $h(X)=E[\tau|X]$.
Controlling for pre-income removes the $X$-induced selection that can flip
Case 2 and leaves a residual association that is monotone in $D$ within
each $X$ stratum. The best linear approximation to a function that is
strictly increasing in $D$ for every $X$, $E[Y|X,D]=m_{0}(X)+D\,h(X)$ with
$h(X)>0$, must load $D$ with a positive coefficient.

The sign-reversal constructions for the linearly controlled regression
require the linear approximation error $v(X)=p(X)-{\rm proj}_{1,X}p(X)$
to be negatively correlated with the non-linear remainder of
$m_{0}(X)+p(X)h(X)$ in an adversarial way and, in the textbook
examples, to rely on ${\rm proj}_{1,X}p(X)$ moving outside the $[0,1]$
probability bounds or on an essentially perfect alignment of the
non-linear part of $m_{0}$ with the non-linear part of $p$. With a
pre-treatment income variable $m_{0}(X)=E[Y_{0}|X]$ is essentially linear
in $X$ and the linear span $\{1,X\}$ already captures the baseline mean.
Under $D\perp Y_{0}|X$ the covariance of the linear approximation error of
$p$ with the baseline mean is absorbed by the linear control, and the
remaining covariance is $E[Var(D|X)h(X)]>0$.

Positivity is therefore guaranteed under unconditional randomisation,
Case 1, and under conditional randomisation once $X$ is linearly
controlled, Case 3, but it is not guaranteed for the marginal
regression under conditional randomisation, Case 2.

4.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The individual effect is $\tau_i=Y_{1i}-Y_{0i}>0$ a.s. and under conditional randomisation $D\perp(Y_0,Y_1)|X$,
$E[Y|X,D]=m_0(X)+D\,h(X)$ with $m_0(X)=E[Y_0|X]$ and $h(X)=E[\tau|X]>0$ a.s.,
$p(X)=E[D|X]$. Then ${\rm Cov}(Y,D|X)=h(X){\rm Var}(D|X)>0$ and the non-parametric partial effect
$E[(D-E[D|X])Y]=E[{\rm Var}(D|X)h(X)]>0$.

Case 1 $D\perp(Y_0,Y_1)$.
$\beta_1=E[Y|D=1]-E[Y|D=0]=E[Y_1]-E[Y_0]=E[\tau]>0$.
Unconditional randomisation gives the ATE, sign forced.

Case 2 $D\perp(Y_0,Y_1)|X$ but $X$ omitted.
$E[Y|D=1]-E[Y|D=0]=E[h(X)|D=1]+E[m_0(X)|D=1]-E[m_0(X)|D=0]$.
Selection $E[m_0|D=1]-E[m_0|D=0]$ is unrestricted. With $p(X)$ decreasing in $m_0(X)$ the bias can dominate, e.g. $X\in\{0,1\}$, $p(0)=1,p(1)=0$, $m_0(0)=0,m_0(1)=100$, $\tau\equiv0.1$ gives $E[Y|D=1]<E[Y|D=0]$. Marginal $1,D$ OLS not signed. This is agreed.

Case 3 $Y$ on $1,D,X$ linear projection. Frisch-Waugh: $\tilde D=D-{\rm proj}_{1,X}D$,
$v(X)=p(X)-{\rm proj}_{1,X}p(X)$.

${\rm Cov}(\tilde D,Y)=E[h(X){\rm Var}(D|X)]+{\rm Cov}\!\big(v(X),m_0(X)+p(X)h(X)\big)$.

The first term $>0$ is the non-parametric partial covariance $E[(D-E[D|X])Y]$. The second term is covariance of the linear-approximation error of $p$ with the possibly non-linear baseline $m_0+p h$. Unconfoundedness does not restrict it. Pointwise ${\rm Cov}(Y,D|X)>0$ does not imply ${\rm Cov}(Y,\tilde D)>0$.

Classic sign reversal: $X=1,2,3$ equiprobable, $m_0(x)=x^2$, $h\equiv0.1$, $p(1)=0.1,p(2)=0.9,p(3)=0.5$. Then $E[Y|X,D]=x^2+0.1D$ is strictly increasing in $D$ for every $X$ and $\tau_i>0$ a.s., yet ${\rm proj}_{1,X}p=0.1+0.2X$, $v=-0.2,0.4,-0.2$, $E[vE[Y|X]]<0$ and ${\rm Cov}(\tilde D,Y)<0$ so $\beta_3<0$. Same with $X\sim U[-1,1]$, $p(x)=0.5+0.4x^2$, $m_0(x)=-k x^2$, $h\equiv0.1$ giving $\beta_3\propto-0.0356k+0.023<0$ for $k\gtrsim1$.

The E camp argues the reversal needs ${\rm proj}_{1,X}p$ to leave $[0,1]$ or an adversarial non-linear $m_0$, and that with a realistic pre-income $m_0$ essentially linear and $p\in[0,1]$ monotone the linear control restores positivity. Under the stated non-parametric set-up no such parametric restriction on $m_0$ or $p$ is allowed. Positivity of the non-parametric residual $D-E[D|X]$ is guaranteed but positivity of the linear residual $D-{\rm proj}_{1,X}D$ is not.

Hence $\tau_i>0$ forces positivity of the unconditional mean difference and of the non-parametric partial effect $E[{\rm Var}(D|X)h(X)]/E[{\rm Var}(D|X)]$, but it does not force positivity of the marginal $1,D$ coefficient under conditional randomisation nor of the linear projection coefficient on $D$ with a linear $X$ control.

Current best belief: only unconditional randomisation guarantees a positive population OLS coefficient on $D$. Cases 2 and 3 can both be sign-reversed. Answer A. Only Case 1.

2.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The model is $Y=Y_{0}+D\tau$, $\tau_i>0$ a.s., $m_{0}(X)=E[Y_{0}|X]$, $h(X)=E[\tau|X]>0$ a.s. Under conditional randomisation $D\perp(Y_{0},\tau)|X$, $E[Y|X,D]=m_{0}(X)+h(X)D$, ${\rm Cov}(Y,D|X)=Var(D|X)h(X)>0$. Non-parametric partial effect $E[(D-E[D|X])Y]=E[Var(D|X)h(X)]>0$.

Case 1 $D\perp(Y_{0},Y_{1})$. $E[Y|D=1]-E[Y|D=0]=E[\tau]>0$. OLS $Y\sim1+D$ is ATE, sign forced. Unanimous.

Case 2 $D\perp(Y_{0},Y_{1})|X$, $X$ omitted. $E[Y|D=1]-E[Y|D=0]=E[h(X)|D=1]+E[m_{0}(X)|D=1]-E[m_{0}(X)|D=0]$. Selection term $Cov(p,m_{0})/Var(D)$ unrestricted. With $p(X)=P(D=1|X)$ decreasing in $m_{0}(X)$ it can dominate $E[h|D=1]$. E.g. $X\in\{0,1\},p(0)=1,p(1)=0,m_{0}(0)=0,m_{0}(1)=100,\tau\equiv0.1$ gives $E[Y|D=1]=0.1<1=E[Y|D=0]$ while $\tau_i>0$ a.s. All colleagues agree sign is not guaranteed.

Case 3 $Y\sim1+D+X$ linear projection. Frisch–Waugh: $\tilde D=D-{\rm proj}_{1,X}D$, $r(X)=p(X)-{\rm proj}_{1,X}p(X)$, $E[r]=E[rX]=0$. 
${\rm Cov}(Y,\tilde D)=E[Var(D|X)h(X)]+{\rm Cov}\big(r(X),m_{0}(X)+p(X)h(X)\big)$.
First term $>0$ is the non-parametric within-$X$ covariance. Second term is covariance of linear-approximation error of propensity with linear-approximation error of $m_{0}+ph$. Unconfoundedness does not restrict it. $Cov(Y,D|X)>0$ pointwise does not imply $Cov(Y,\tilde D)>0$.

Explicit sign reversal: $X=1,2,3$ equiprobable, $m_{0}(x)=x^{2}$, $h\equiv0.1$, $p(1)=0.1,p(2)=0.9,p(3)=0.5$. Then $E[Y|X,D]=x^{2}+0.1D$ strictly increasing in $D$ for every $X$, $\tau_i>0$ a.s., ${\rm proj}_{1,X}p=0.1+0.2X$, $r=-0.2,0.4,-0.2$, and $E[rE[Y|X]]<0$ so ${\rm Cov}(Y,\tilde D)<0$ and $\beta_{3}<0$. Same with $X\sim U[-1,1]$, $p(x)=0.5+0.4x^{2}$, $m_{0}(x)=-k x^{2}$ giving $b\propto-0.0356k+0.023<0$ for $k\gtrsim1$.

The E camp – Colleagues 1,5,7,9,13,14 – argues positivity is restored by linear control, claiming $\beta_{3}$ is a positive weighted average of $h(X)$ and that $Cov(r,m_{0})$ is absorbed or negligible when $p\in[0,1]$ and $m_{0}$ is essentially linear/monotone as for pre-income. They implicitly add regularity: ${\rm proj}_{1,X}p$ stays in $[0,1]$ and $m_{0}$ is close to linear, i.e. an extra parametric restriction not allowed.

The A camp – Colleagues 10,11,12,2,3,4,6,8 – keeps the non-parametric setting: $m_{0}$ and $p$ are unrestricted non-linear functions, ${\rm proj}_{1,X}p$ can leave $[0,1]$, and $Cov(r,m_{0}+ph)$ can be made arbitrarily negative to dominate $E[Var(D|X)h(X)]$. Hence the linear residual $D-{\rm proj}_{1,X}D$ is not mean independent of $X$ and sign reversal is possible.

Current belief unchanged: positivity of $\tau_i>0$ a.s. forces positivity only under unconditional randomisation. Case 2 and Case 3 can both be sign-reversed under the stated non-parametric assumptions. Therefore answer A: Only Case 1.

Unresolved tension remains between the mathematical counterexample and the economic “feasibility” intuition that $proj_{1,X}p$ should stay in $[0,1]$ and $m_{0}$ monotone linear-ish, but that is an extra restriction beyond unconfoundedness + $\tau>0$.

3.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The population OLS coefficient is the linear projection of Y on the regressors. Write Y = Y0 + D τ with τ>0 a.s., m0(X)=E[Y0|X], h(X)=E[τ|X]>0 a.s., p(X)=E[D|X]. Under conditional randomisation D ⟂ (Y0,τ)|X, E[Y|X,D]=m0(X)+h(X)D and Cov(Y,D|X)=h(X)Var(D|X)>0 pointwise. The non-parametric partial effect E[(D-E[D|X])Y]=E[Var(D|X)h(X)]>0 is always positive.

Case 1. D ⟂ (Y0,Y1). β1 = E[Y|D=1]-E[Y|D=0]=E[Y1]-E[Y0]=E[τ]>0. Unconditional randomisation identifies the ATE and the sign is forced non-parametrically. No dispute.

Case 2. D ⟂ (Y0,Y1)|X but X is omitted. E[Y|D=1]-E[Y|D=0]=E[h(X)|D=1]+E[m0(X)|D=1]-E[m0(X)|D=0]. The selection term Cov(p,m0)/Var(D) is unrestricted by unconfoundedness. With p(X) decreasing in m0(X) the bias can dominate E[h|D=1]. e.g. X∈{0,1}, p0=1,p1=0,m0(0)=0,m0(1)=100, τ≡0.1 gives E[Y|D=1]=0.1<1=E[Y|D=0] while τ>0 a.s. Sign not guaranteed. Consensus.

Case 3. Y∼1+D+X. Let D̃=D-proj_{1,X}D, r(X)=p(X)-proj_{1,X}p(X), E[r]=E[rX]=0. Then
Cov(Y,D̃)=E[Var(D|X)h(X)]+Cov(r(X),m0(X)+p(X)h(X)).
First term >0. Second term is covariance of the linear-approximation error of the propensity with the linear-approximation error of E[Y|X]. Unconfoundedness does not restrict it. Pointwise Cov(Y,D|X)>0 does not imply Cov(Y,D̃)>0.

Counterexamples: X=1,2,3 equiprobable, m0(x)=x², h≡0.1, p(1)=0.1,p(2)=0.9,p(3)=0.5 gives proj_{1,X}p=0.1+0.2X, r=-0.2,0.4,-0.2 and Cov(Y,D̃)<0 while E[Y|D=1,X]-E[Y|D=0,X]=h>0 a.s. Same with X∼U[-1,1], p(x)=0.5+0.4x², m0(x)=-k x², h≡0.1 giving β3<0 for k large. The error is confusing the non-parametric residual D-E[D|X] with the linear residual D-proj_{1,X}D; Cov(D̃,m0)≠0 when m0 is non-linear.

The E camp argues Case 3 must be positive because conditional mean is increasing in D for each X and controlling for X removes selection, with the additional informal restriction that m0 is essentially monotone/linear in pre-income and p∈[0,1] stays in the linear span. That is an extra realism restriction not given: “Do not make any parametric assumptions beyond what I have given.” The problem gives only positivity of τ, binary D, continuous Y, controls X. Under those non-parametric assumptions the linear projection can be signed the wrong way by selection on X and by linear misspecification of E[Y0|X].

Current belief remains: positivity is guaranteed only under unconditional randomisation. Option A. Only Case 1. Case 2 and Case 3 are both sign unidentified non-parametrically. The remaining disagreement in the group is exactly the distinction between non-parametric partial covariance E[Var(D|X)h]>0 and the linear residual covariance Cov(Y,D̃) which can be negative.

11.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The core structure is unchanged: Y = Y0 + D τ, τi>0 a.s., E[Y|X,D]=m0(X)+D h(X) with h(X)=E[τ|X]>0 a.s., D⊥(Y0,τ)|X, p(X)=E[D|X], m0(X)=E[Y0|X].

Case 1 D⊥(Y0,Y1). β1=E[Y|D=1]-E[Y|D=0]=E[Y1]-E[Y0]=E[τ]>0. Uncontroversial. All agree.

Case 2 D⊥(Y0,Y1)|X but X omitted. E[Y|D=1]-E[Y|D=0]=E[h(X)|D=1]+E[m0(X)|D=1]-E[m0(X)|D=0]. Selection term Cov(p,m0)/Var(D) is unrestricted. Discrete example X∈{0,1}, p0=1,p1=0,m0(0)=0,m0(1)=100, τ≡0.1 gives E[Y|D=1]=0.1<1=E[Y|D=0] despite τ>0 a.s. Consensus that marginal constant-D regression is not sign guaranteed.

Case 3 Y regressed on 1,D,X linearly. Frisch-Waugh β_D =Cov(Y,D̃)/Var(D̃) with D̃=D - proj_{1,X}D. Non-parametric residual D - E[D|X] satisfies E[(D-E[D|X])Y]=E[Var(D|X)h(X)]>0. The linear residual is different.

E[D̃ Y]=E[E[D̃|X]E[Y|X]]+E[Var(D|X)h(X)]. E[D̃ Y|X]=E[D̃|X]E[Y|X]+Var(D|X)h(X). Hence Cov(Y,D̃)=E[Var(D|X)h(X)]+Cov(p-proj p, m0+ p h). First term >0, second term unrestricted.

Explicit counterexample: X=1,2,3 equiprobable, m0(x)=x², h≡0.1>0, p(1)=0.1,p(2)=0.9,p(3)=0.5. proj_{1,X}p =0.1+0.2X, r(x)=p-proj= -0.2,0.4,-0.2. Then E[Y|X,D]=x²+0.1D strictly increasing in D for every X, τ>0 a.s., yet E[r E[Y|X]]<0 and Cov(Y,D̃)<0 so β3<0. Same with X∈{-1,0,1}, m0=x², p(-1)=0.1,p(0)=0.9,p(1)=0.5 etc. Also X~U[-1,1], p(x)=0.5+0.4x², m0(x)=-k x², h≡0.1 gives β∝ -0.0356k+0.023 negative for k large.

Hence pointwise Cov(Y,D|X)=Var(D|X)h(X)>0 does not imply Cov(Y,D̃)>0 for linear residual. The sign reversal is classic Simpson reversal due to non-linear m0 and/or non-linear p.

The E camp argues positivity must hold for case3 because conditional mean is monotone in D and the linear control removes selection, claiming β3 is a positive weighted average of h(X). Argument relies on an implicit restriction that proj_{1,X}p stays in [0,1] and that m0 is essentially linear/monotone in X, i.e. a parametric/monotone feasibility restriction. Under the stated “no parametric assumptions beyond what I have given” that restriction is not allowed; the three-point example respects p∈[0,1] and D⊥(Y0,τ)|X with τ>0 a.s.

The disagreement in round 3 is exactly this: colleagues 1,13,14 etc maintain realistic income monotonicity makes case3 positive; colleagues 10,11,12,2,3,4,6,8 maintain formal non-parametric counterexample stands and the only guaranteed sign is unconditional randomisation.

Current belief remains A. Only Case 1 must be positive. Cases 2 and 3 can be sign reversed by selection on X and by linear misspecification of m0 and p. The non-parametric partial effect E[(D-E[D|X])Y]>0 is guaranteed, but the linear projection coefficient is not. Unresolved nuance is whether the three-point counterexample is deemed admissible under the “jobs programme” concreteness; formally it is admissible under non-parametric assumptions.

6.text:

Case 3 $Y$ on $1,D,X$ linear projection. Frisch-Waugh: $\tilde D=D-{\rm proj}_{1,X}D$, $v(X)=p(X)-{\rm proj}_{1,X}p(X)$, $E[v]=E[vX]=0$. Then
$Cov(Y,\tilde D)=E[Var(D|X)h(X)]+Cov\big(v(X),m_{0}(X)+p(X)h(X)\big)$.
First term $>0$. Second term is covariance of the linear-approximation error of $p$ with the possibly non-linear $m_{0}+ph$. Unconfoundedness does not restrict it. Pointwise $Cov(Y,D|X)>0$ does not imply $Cov(Y,\tilde D)>0$.

Explicit sign reversals exist with non-linear $m_{0}$ and $p$. E.g. $X=1,2,3$ equiprobable, $m_{0}(x)=x^{2}$, $h\equiv0.1$, $p(1)=0.1,p(2)=0.9,p(3)=0.5$. Same construction with $X\sim U[-1,1]$, $p(x)=\mathbf1\{x\ge0\}$, $h(x)=e^{\lambda x}$ gives ${\rm proj}_{X}p>1$ where $h$ is largest and linear coefficient negative.

The E camp argues $E[\tilde D Y|X]=Var(D|X)h(X)>0$ after linear partialling and that $E[Y|D=1,X]>E[Y|D=0,X]$ for every $X$ forces a positive linear slope. Under the problem’s stated “no parametric assumptions beyond what I have given” that restriction is not allowed; $m_{0}$ and $p$ can be any measurable functions with $p\in[0,1]$.

Hence positivity is guaranteed only under unconditional randomisation. Cases 2 and 3 can both be sign reversed by $X$-dependent propensity and non-linear $m_{0}/p$; the classic linear Simpson reversal applies to Case 3. Current best non-parametric assessment is Answer A. Only Case 1, with the understanding that the disagreement in round 3 is precisely about whether the linear-approximation error term can be made arbitrarily negative under the stated non-parametric conditions, and the counterexamples above show it can.

reflection_text.4:
The individual effect is $\tau_i=Y_{1i}-Y_{0i}>0$ a.s. and under conditional randomisation $D\perp(Y_0,Y_1)|X$,
$E[Y|X,D]=m_0(X)+D\,h(X)$ with $m_0(X)=E[Y_0|X]$ and $h(X)=E[\tau|X]>0$ a.s.,
$p(X)=E[D|X]$. Then ${\rm Cov}(Y,D|X)=h(X){\rm Var}(D|X)>0$ and the non-parametric partial effect
$E[(D-E[D|X])Y]=E[{\rm Var}(D|X)h(X)]>0$.

Case 1 $D\perp(Y_0,Y_1)$.
$\beta_1=E[Y|D=1]-E[Y|D=0]=E[Y_1]-E[Y_0]=E[\tau]>0$.
Unconditional randomisation gives the ATE, sign forced.

Case 2 $D\perp(Y_0,Y_1)|X$ but $X$ omitted.
$E[Y|D=1]-E[Y|D=0]=E[h(X)|D=1]+E[m_0(X)|D=1]-E[m_0(X)|D=0]$.
Selection $E[m_0|D=1]-E[m_0|D=0]$ is unrestricted. With $p(X)$ decreasing in $m_0(X)$ the bias can dominate, e.g. $X\in\{0,1\}$, $p(0)=1,p(1)=0$, $m_0(0)=0,m_0(1)=100$, $\tau\equiv0.1$ gives $E[Y|D=1]<E[Y|D=0]$. Marginal $1,D$ OLS not signed. This is agreed.

Case 3 $Y$ on $1,D,X$ linear projection. Frisch-Waugh: $\tilde D=D-{\rm proj}_{1,X}D$,
$v(X)=p(X)-{\rm proj}_{1,X}p(X)$.

${\rm Cov}(\tilde D,Y)=E[h(X){\rm Var}(D|X)]+{\rm Cov}\!\big(v(X),m_0(X)+p(X)h(X)\big)$.

The first term $>0$ is the non-parametric partial covariance $E[(D-E[D|X])Y]$. The second term is covariance of the linear-approximation error of $p$ with the possibly non-linear baseline $m_0+p h$. Unconfoundedness does not restrict it. Pointwise ${\rm Cov}(Y,D|X)>0$ does not imply ${\rm Cov}(Y,\tilde D)>0$.

Classic sign reversal: $X=1,2,3$ equiprobable, $m_0(x)=x^2$, $h\equiv0.1$, $p(1)=0.1,p(2)=0.9,p(3)=0.5$. Then $E[Y|X,D]=x^2+0.1D$ is strictly increasing in $D$ for every $X$ and $\tau_i>0$ a.s., yet ${\rm proj}_{1,X}p=0.1+0.2X$, $v=-0.2,0.4,-0.2$, $E[vE[Y|X]]<0$ and ${\rm Cov}(\tilde D,Y)<0$ so $\beta_3<0$. Same with $X\sim U[-1,1]$, $p(x)=0.5+0.4x^2$, $m_0(x)=-k x^2$, $h\equiv0.1$ giving $\beta_3\propto-0.0356k+0.023<0$ for $k\gtrsim1$.

The E camp argues the reversal needs ${\rm proj}_{1,X}p$ to leave $[0,1]$ or an adversarial non-linear $m_0$, and that with a realistic pre-income $m_0$ essentially linear and $p\in[0,1]$ monotone the linear control restores positivity. Under the stated non-parametric set-up no such parametric restriction on $m_0$ or $p$ is allowed. Positivity of the non-parametric residual $D-E[D|X]$ is guaranteed but positivity of the linear residual $D-{\rm proj}_{1,X}D$ is not.

Hence $\tau_i>0$ forces positivity of the unconditional mean difference and of the non-parametric partial effect $E[{\rm Var}(D|X)h(X)]/E[{\rm Var}(D|X)]$, but it does not force positivity of the marginal $1,D$ coefficient under conditional randomisation nor of the linear projection coefficient on $D$ with a linear $X$ control.

Current best belief: only unconditional randomisation guarantees a positive population OLS coefficient on $D$. Cases 2 and 3 can both be sign-reversed. Answer A. Only Case 1.
reflection_text.2:
The model is $Y=Y_{0}+D\tau$, $\tau_i>0$ a.s., $m_{0}(X)=E[Y_{0}|X]$, $h(X)=E[\tau|X]>0$ a.s. Under conditional randomisation $D\perp(Y_{0},\tau)|X$, $E[Y|X,D]=m_{0}(X)+h(X)D$, ${\rm Cov}(Y,D|X)=Var(D|X)h(X)>0$. Non-parametric partial effect $E[(D-E[D|X])Y]=E[Var(D|X)h(X)]>0$.

Case 1 $D\perp(Y_{0},Y_{1})$. $E[Y|D=1]-E[Y|D=0]=E[\tau]>0$. OLS $Y\sim1+D$ is ATE, sign forced. Unanimous.

Case 2 $D\perp(Y_{0},Y_{1})|X$, $X$ omitted. $E[Y|D=1]-E[Y|D=0]=E[h(X)|D=1]+E[m_{0}(X)|D=1]-E[m_{0}(X)|D=0]$. Selection term $Cov(p,m_{0})/Var(D)$ unrestricted. With $p(X)=P(D=1|X)$ decreasing in $m_{0}(X)$ it can dominate $E[h|D=1]$. E.g. $X\in\{0,1\},p(0)=1,p(1)=0,m_{0}(0)=0,m_{0}(1)=100,\tau\equiv0.1$ gives $E[Y|D=1]=0.1<1=E[Y|D=0]$ while $\tau_i>0$ a.s. All colleagues agree sign is not guaranteed.

Case 3 $Y\sim1+D+X$ linear projection. Frisch–Waugh: $\tilde D=D-{\rm proj}_{1,X}D$, $r(X)=p(X)-{\rm proj}_{1,X}p(X)$, $E[r]=E[rX]=0$. 
${\rm Cov}(Y,\tilde D)=E[Var(D|X)h(X)]+{\rm Cov}\big(r(X),m_{0}(X)+p(X)h(X)\big)$.
First term $>0$ is the non-parametric within-$X$ covariance. Second term is covariance of linear-approximation error of propensity with linear-approximation error of $m_{0}+ph$. Unconfoundedness does not restrict it. $Cov(Y,D|X)>0$ pointwise does not imply $Cov(Y,\tilde D)>0$.

Explicit sign reversal: $X=1,2,3$ equiprobable, $m_{0}(x)=x^{2}$, $h\equiv0.1$, $p(1)=0.1,p(2)=0.9,p(3)=0.5$. Then $E[Y|X,D]=x^{2}+0.1D$ strictly increasing in $D$ for every $X$, $\tau_i>0$ a.s., ${\rm proj}_{1,X}p=0.1+0.2X$, $r=-0.2,0.4,-0.2$, and $E[rE[Y|X]]<0$ so ${\rm Cov}(Y,\tilde D)<0$ and $\beta_{3}<0$. Same with $X\sim U[-1,1]$, $p(x)=0.5+0.4x^{2}$, $m_{0}(x)=-k x^{2}$ giving $b\propto-0.0356k+0.023<0$ for $k\gtrsim1$.

The E camp – Colleagues 1,5,7,9,13,14 – argues positivity is restored by linear control, claiming $\beta_{3}$ is a positive weighted average of $h(X)$ and that $Cov(r,m_{0})$ is absorbed or negligible when $p\in[0,1]$ and $m_{0}$ is essentially linear/monotone as for pre-income. They implicitly add regularity: ${\rm proj}_{1,X}p$ stays in $[0,1]$ and $m_{0}$ is close to linear, i.e. an extra parametric restriction not allowed.

The A camp – Colleagues 10,11,12,2,3,4,6,8 – keeps the non-parametric setting: $m_{0}$ and $p$ are unrestricted non-linear functions, ${\rm proj}_{1,X}p$ can leave $[0,1]$, and $Cov(r,m_{0}+ph)$ can be made arbitrarily negative to dominate $E[Var(D|X)h(X)]$. Hence the linear residual $D-{\rm proj}_{1,X}D$ is not mean independent of $X$ and sign reversal is possible.

Current belief unchanged: positivity of $\tau_i>0$ a.s. forces positivity only under unconditional randomisation. Case 2 and Case 3 can both be sign-reversed under the stated non-parametric assumptions. Therefore answer A: Only Case 1.

Unresolved tension remains between the mathematical counterexample and the economic “feasibility” intuition that $proj_{1,X}p$ should stay in $[0,1]$ and $m_{0}$ monotone linear-ish, but that is an extra restriction beyond unconfoundedness + $\tau>0$.
reflection_text.3:
The population OLS coefficient is the linear projection of Y on the regressors. Write Y = Y0 + D τ with τ>0 a.s., m0(X)=E[Y0|X], h(X)=E[τ|X]>0 a.s., p(X)=E[D|X]. Under conditional randomisation D ⟂ (Y0,τ)|X, E[Y|X,D]=m0(X)+h(X)D and Cov(Y,D|X)=h(X)Var(D|X)>0 pointwise. The non-parametric partial effect E[(D-E[D|X])Y]=E[Var(D|X)h(X)]>0 is always positive.

Case 1. D ⟂ (Y0,Y1). β1 = E[Y|D=1]-E[Y|D=0]=E[Y1]-E[Y0]=E[τ]>0. Unconditional randomisation identifies the ATE and the sign is forced non-parametrically. No dispute.

Case 2. D ⟂ (Y0,Y1)|X but X is omitted. E[Y|D=1]-E[Y|D=0]=E[h(X)|D=1]+E[m0(X)|D=1]-E[m0(X)|D=0]. The selection term Cov(p,m0)/Var(D) is unrestricted by unconfoundedness. With p(X) decreasing in m0(X) the bias can dominate E[h|D=1]. e.g. X∈{0,1}, p0=1,p1=0,m0(0)=0,m0(1)=100, τ≡0.1 gives E[Y|D=1]=0.1<1=E[Y|D=0] while τ>0 a.s. Sign not guaranteed. Consensus.

Case 3. Y∼1+D+X. Let D̃=D-proj_{1,X}D, r(X)=p(X)-proj_{1,X}p(X), E[r]=E[rX]=0. Then
Cov(Y,D̃)=E[Var(D|X)h(X)]+Cov(r(X),m0(X)+p(X)h(X)).
First term >0. Second term is covariance of the linear-approximation error of the propensity with the linear-approximation error of E[Y|X]. Unconfoundedness does not restrict it. Pointwise Cov(Y,D|X)>0 does not imply Cov(Y,D̃)>0.

Counterexamples: X=1,2,3 equiprobable, m0(x)=x², h≡0.1, p(1)=0.1,p(2)=0.9,p(3)=0.5 gives proj_{1,X}p=0.1+0.2X, r=-0.2,0.4,-0.2 and Cov(Y,D̃)<0 while E[Y|D=1,X]-E[Y|D=0,X]=h>0 a.s. Same with X∼U[-1,1], p(x)=0.5+0.4x², m0(x)=-k x², h≡0.1 giving β3<0 for k large. The error is confusing the non-parametric residual D-E[D|X] with the linear residual D-proj_{1,X}D; Cov(D̃,m0)≠0 when m0 is non-linear.

The E camp argues Case 3 must be positive because conditional mean is increasing in D for each X and controlling for X removes selection, with the additional informal restriction that m0 is essentially monotone/linear in pre-income and p∈[0,1] stays in the linear span. That is an extra realism restriction not given: “Do not make any parametric assumptions beyond what I have given.” The problem gives only positivity of τ, binary D, continuous Y, controls X. Under those non-parametric assumptions the linear projection can be signed the wrong way by selection on X and by linear misspecification of E[Y0|X].

Current belief remains: positivity is guaranteed only under unconditional randomisation. Option A. Only Case 1. Case 2 and Case 3 are both sign unidentified non-parametrically. The remaining disagreement in the group is exactly the distinction between non-parametric partial covariance E[Var(D|X)h]>0 and the linear residual covariance Cov(Y,D̃) which can be negative.

reflection_text.6:

reflection_text.10:
The model is Y = Y0 + D τ, τ>0 a.s., D ⟂ (Y0,τ)|X, so E[Y|X,D]=m0(X)+D h(X) with h(X)=E[τ|X]>0 a.s., p(X)=E[D|X]. Case1 unconditional randomisation: β1=E[Y|D=1]-E[Y|D=0]=E[τ]>0. Unanimous.

Case2 marginal regression under conditional randomisation: E[Y|D=1]-E[Y|D=0]=E[h|X,D=1]+E[m0|X,D=1]-E[m0|X,D=0]. Selection on X is unrestricted by D⟂·|X. With p decreasing in m0 the sign can be made arbitrarily negative, e.g. p(0)=1,p(1)=0,m0(0)=0,m0(1)=100,τ≡0.1 gives E[Y|D=1]<E[Y|D=0]. Everyone agrees Case2 is not signed.

Case3 Y on 1,D,X linear projection. Let D̃ = D - proj_{1,X}D, r(X)=p(X)-proj_{1,X}p(X). Then
Cov(Y,D̃)=E[Var(D|X)h(X)]+Cov(r(X),m0(X)+p(X)h(X)).
The first term >0. The second term is covariance of the linear-approximation error of p with the linear-approximation error of m0+p h. Unconfoundedness does not restrict it. Pointwise Cov(Y,D|X)=Var(D|X)h(X)>0 does not imply Cov(Y,D̃)>0.

Explicit non-parametric reversals exist with no parametric restriction:
X∈{1,2,3} equiprobable, m0(x)=x², h≡0.1, p(1)=0.1,p(2)=0.9,p(3)=0.5. Then E[Y|X,D]=x²+0.1D is strictly increasing in D for every X, τ>0 a.s., D⟂(Y0,τ)|X, proj_{1,X}p=0.1+0.2X∈[0,1], r=-0.2,0.4,-0.2, and Cov(Y,D̃)<0 so the Frisch-Waugh coefficient β3<0. Same with X∈{-1,0,1} equiprobable, m0=x², h≡0.1, p(-1)=0.1,p(0)=0.9,p(1)=0.5.

The non-parametric residual D-E[D|X] is guaranteed positive: E[(D-E[D|X])Y]=E[Var(D|X)h(X)]>0. Positivity fails for the linear residual D-proj_{1,X}D because the linear space {1,X} does not span non-linear m0 and p. The E camp argues positivity is restored by linear control, claiming β3 is a positive weighted average of h(X) and that for a jobs programme m0 is essentially linear and p∈[0,1] so the second covariance term is second order. That is a parametric/feasibility restriction not allowed by “no parametric assumptions beyond what I have given”. The counterexamples above keep proj_{1,X}p in [0,1] and still reverse sign.

Thus my current belief remains A. Only Case1 must be positive in the population. Case2 can be negative by marginal selection on X, and Case3 can be negative by linear misspecification of m0 and p, i.e. a Simpson-type reversal of the linear projection even though E[Y|D=1,X]-E[Y|D=0,X]=h(X)>0 for all X. The disagreement in the current round is between colleagues 1,5,7,9,13,14 claiming positivity is restored by linear control and colleagues 10,11,12,2,3,4,6,8 giving explicit sign reversals for Case3. Unresolved nuance is the appeal to economic plausibility of monotone linear m0/p versus the formal non-parametric allowance.
reflection_text.12:
The individual effect τ_i=Y1i−Y0i>0 a.s. and under conditional randomisation E[Y|X,D]=m0(X)+D τ(X) with τ(X)=E[τ|X]>0, p(X)=E[D|X].

Case 1: D⊥(Y0,Y1). β1=E[Y|D=1]−E[Y|D=0]=E[Y1]−E[Y0]=E[τ]>0. Unconditional randomisation forces a positive population difference in means. Unanimous.

Case 2: D⊥(Y0,Y1)|X but D may depend on X. 
E[Y|D=1]−E[Y|D=0]=E[τ(X)|D=1]+E[m0(X)|D=1]−E[m0(X)|D=0].
The first term >0 but selection term E[m0|D=1]−E[m0|D=0] is unrestricted. With p(X) decreasing in m0(X) the bias can dominate, e.g. X∈{0,1}, p0=1,p1=0, m0(0)=0,m0(1)=100, τ≡0.1 gives E[Y|D=1]=0.1<1=E[Y|D=0]. Everyone now agrees the marginal 1,D slope is not signed.

Case 3: linear projection Y on 1,D,X. Let proj_{1,X}D = α+βX and r(X)=p(X)−α−βX. Frisch-Waugh gives β3∝Cov(Y,tilde D) with tilde D=D−proj_{1,X}D.
Cov(Y,tilde D)=E[Var(D|X)τ(X)]+Cov(r(X), m0(X)+p(X)τ(X)).
The first term >0 is the non-parametric within-X partial covariance E[(D−E[D|X])Y]>0.
The second term is the covariance of the linear approximation error of the propensity with the possibly non-linear baseline m0(X)+p(X)τ(X). Unconfoundedness does not restrict it.

Pointwise E[Y|D=1,X]−E[Y|D=0,X]=τ(X)>0 and Cov(Y,D|X)=Var(D|X)τ(X)>0 do not imply Cov(Y,tilde D)>0. The linear residual D−proj_{1,X}D is not mean independent of X, so it can proxy the non-linear part of m0.

Concrete counter-examples:
X=1,2,3 equiprobable, m0(x)=x², τ≡0.1>0, p(1)=0.1,p(2)=0.9,p(3)=0.5. proj_{1,X}p=0.1+0.2X, r=−0.2,0.4,−0.2 and E[r m0]<0 enough to make Cov(Y,tilde D)<0 while τ>0 a.s. and E[Y|X,D]=x²+0.1D is strictly increasing in D for each X.
Same with X∼U[−1,1], p(x)=0.5+0.4x², m0(x)=−k x², τ≡0.1 → β∝−0.0356k+0.023<0 for k large.

The E camp argues the sign reversal requires proj_{1,X}p to leave [0,1] and an adversarial alignment of non-linear m0 with v(X)=p−proj p, and that with a realistic monotone pre-income baseline and propensity staying in [0,1] the linear control suffices, giving β3 as a positive weighted average of τ(X). That is an extra parametric/regularity restriction.

Under the stated non-parametric assumptions — no restriction on m0(·) and p(·) beyond D⊥(Y0,Y1)|X and τ_i>0 — the linear approximation error can be made arbitrarily negatively correlated with m0, so positivity of the linear projection is not guaranteed. The non-parametric partial effect using D−E[D|X] is always positive, the linear projection is not.

Hence the only case non-parametrically forced positive is unconditional randomisation. Current belief remains A. Only Case 1 must be positive. Case 2 and the linearly controlled Case 3 can both be sign reversed by X-dependent randomisation and linear misspecification of m0. The split in the room is the classic confusion between Cov(Y,D|X)>0 and positivity of the linear projection coefficient when m0 is non-linear.
reflection_text.8:
The persistent potential-outcomes model is $Y=Y_{0}+D\tau$, $\tau_i>0$ a.s., $E[Y|X,D]=m_{0}(X)+D\,h(X)$ with $h(X)=E[\tau|X]>0$ a.s., $D\perp(Y_{0},\tau)|X$, $p(X)=E[D|X]$. Conditional randomisation gives $Cov(Y,D|X)=Var(D|X)h(X)>0$ pointwise and the non-parametric partial covariance $E[(D-E[D|X])Y]=E[Var(D|X)h(X)]>0$.

Case 1 $D\perp(Y_{0},Y_{1})$. $\beta_{1}=E[Y|D=1]-E[Y|D=0]=E[Y_{1}-Y_{0}]=E[\tau]>0$. Unconditional randomisation forces OLS $1,D$ to be the ATE. Guaranteed.

Case 2 $D\perp(Y_{0},Y_{1})|X$ but $X$ omitted. $E[Y|D=1]-E[Y|D=0]=E[h(X)|D=1]+E[m_{0}(X)|D=1]-E[m_{0}(X)|D=0]$. The selection term $E[m_{0}|D=1]-E[m_{0}|D=0]=Cov(p,m_{0})/Var(D)$ is unrestricted. With $p(X)$ decreasing in $m_{0}(X)$ the bias can dominate $E[h|D=1]$. E.g. $X\in\{0,1\},p(0)=1,p(1)=0,m_{0}(0)=0,m_{0}(1)=100,\tau\equiv0.1$ gives $E[Y|D=1]<E[Y|D=0]$ while $\tau>0$ a.s. Not guaranteed.

Case 3 $Y$ on $1,D,X$ linear projection. Frisch-Waugh: $\tilde D=D-{\rm proj}_{1,X}D$, $v(X)=p(X)-{\rm proj}_{1,X}p(X)$, $E[v]=E[vX]=0$. Then
$Cov(Y,\tilde D)=E[Var(D|X)h(X)]+Cov\big(v(X),m_{0}(X)+p(X)h(X)\big)$.
First term $>0$. Second term is covariance of the linear-approximation error of $p$ with the possibly non-linear $m_{0}+ph$. Unconfoundedness does not restrict it. Pointwise $Cov(Y,D|X)>0$ does not imply $Cov(Y,\tilde D)>0$.

Explicit sign reversals exist with non-linear $m_{0}$ and $p$. E.g. $X=1,2,3$ equiprobable, $m_{0}(x)=x^{2}$, $h\equiv0.1$, $p(1)=0.1,p(2)=0.9,p(3)=0.5$. Then $E[Y|X,D]=x^{2}+0.1D$ is strictly increasing in $D$ for every $X$, $\tau>0$ a.s., ${\rm proj}_{1,X}p=0.1+0.2X$, $v=-0.2,0.4,-0.2$, $E[vE[Y|X]]<0$ so $Cov(\tilde D,Y)<0$ and $\beta_{D}<0$. Same construction with $X\sim U[-1,1]$, $p(x)=\mathbf1\{x\ge0\}$, $h(x)=e^{\lambda x}$ gives ${\rm proj}_{X}p>1$ where $h$ is largest and linear coefficient negative.

The E camp argues $E[\tilde D Y|X]=Var(D|X)h(X)>0$ after linear partialling and that $E[Y|D=1,X]>E[Y|D=0,X]$ for every $X$ forces a positive linear slope. That holds for the non-parametric residual $D-E[D|X]$ but not for the linear residual $D-{\rm proj}_{1,X}D$. Their defence invokes realistic restrictions: $m_{0}$ monotone and essentially linear in pre-income and $p\in[0,1]$ monotone, so $proj_{1,X}p$ stays in $[0,1]$ and $Cov(v,m_{0}+ph)$ is second order. Under the problem’s stated “no parametric assumptions beyond what I have given” that restriction is not allowed; $m_{0}$ and $p$ can be any measurable functions with $p\in[0,1]$.

Hence positivity is guaranteed only under unconditional randomisation. Cases 2 and 3 can both be sign reversed by $X$-dependent propensity and non-linear $m_{0}/p$; the classic linear Simpson reversal applies to Case 3. Current best non-parametric assessment is Answer A. Only Case 1, with the understanding that the disagreement in round 3 is precisely about whether the linear-approximation error term can be made arbitrarily negative under the stated non-parametric conditions, and the counterexamples above show it can.

2.text:
With $Y=Y_{0}+D\tau$, $\tau_{i}>0$ a.s., $m_{0}(X)=E[Y_{0}|X]$,
$h(X)=E[\tau|X]>0$ a.s., $p(X)=E[D|X]$ and under conditional
randomisation

$D\!\perp\!(Y_{0},\tau)|X$,
$E[Y|X,D]=m_{0}(X)+h(X)D$,
${\rm Cov}(Y,D|X)=Var(D|X)h(X)>0$ a.s.

The non-parametric partial effect is
$E[(D-E[D|X])Y]=E[Var(D|X)h(X)]>0$.

Case 1. $D\perp(Y_{0},Y_{1})$.
$\beta_{1}=E[Y|D=1]-E[Y|D=0]=E[Y_{1}-Y_{0}]=E[\tau]>0$.
The $1,D$ OLS is the ATE and is non-parametrically forced positive.

Case 2. $D\perp(Y_{0},Y_{1})|X$ but $X$ omitted.
$E[Y|D=1]-E[Y|D=0]=E[h(X)|D=1]+E[m_{0}(X)|D=1]-E[m_{0}(X)|D=0]$.
The selection term $E[m_{0}|D=1]-E[m_{0}|D=0]=Cov(p,m_{0})/Var(D)$ is
unrestricted by unconfoundedness. With $p(x)$ decreasing in $m_{0}(x)$ it
can dominate $E[h|D=1]$. E.g. $X\in\{0,1\},p(0)=1,p(1)=0$,
$m_{0}(0)=0,m_{0}(1)=100,\tau\equiv0.1$ gives
$E[Y|D=1]=0.1<1=E[Y|D=0]$ although $\tau_{i}>0$ a.s. The marginal $1,D$
slope is not signed.

Case 3. $Y\sim1+D+X$ is the linear projection. Let
$\tilde D=D-{\rm proj}_{1,X}D$, $r(X)=p(X)-{\rm proj}_{1,X}p(X)$,
$E[r]=E[rX]=0$. Then

${\rm Cov}(Y,\tilde D)=E[Var(D|X)h(X)]+{\rm Cov}\!\big(r(X),m_{0}(X)+p(X)h(X)\big)$,
$\beta_{3}={\rm Cov}(Y,\tilde D)/Var(\tilde D)$.

$E[Var(D|X)h(X)]>0$ is the non-parametric within-$X$ term. The second
term is the covariance of the linear approximation error of the propensity
with the possibly non-linear function $m_{0}(X)+p(X)h(X)$. Unconfoundedness
does not restrict it. Pointwise $E[Y|D=1,X]-E[Y|D=0,X]=h(X)>0$ does not
imply ${\rm Cov}(Y,\tilde D)>0$.

E.g. $X=1,2,3$ equiprobable, $m_{0}(x)=x^{2}$, $h\equiv0.1>0$,
$p(1)=0.1,p(2)=0.9,p(3)=0.5$. Then $E[Y|X,D]=x^{2}+0.1D$ is strictly
increasing in $D$ for every $X$ and $\tau_{i}>0$ a.s.,
${\rm proj}_{1,X}p=0.1+0.2X$, $r=-0.2,0.4,-0.2$ and
$E[rE[Y|X]]<0$. Hence ${\rm Cov}(Y,\tilde D)<0$ and $\beta_{3}<0$ in the
population regression $Y=\alpha+\beta_{D}D+\gamma X+u$ while
$E[Y|D=1,X]-E[Y|D=0,X]=h(X)>0$ a.s.

The same reversal is obtained with $X\sim U[-1,1]$,
$p(x)=0.5+0.4x^{2}$, $m_{0}(x)=-k x^{2}$ with $k$ large enough.
Positivity of $E[(D-E[D|X])Y]$ is guaranteed, but positivity of the
linear residual $D-{\rm proj}_{1,X}D$ is not.

Hence $\tau_{i}>0$ a.s. forces positivity of the unconditionally
randomised mean difference, and of the non-parametric partial covariance,
but it does not force positivity of the marginal regression under
conditional randomisation nor of the best linear approximation $Y\sim1+D+X$
without further regularity on $m_{0}$ and $p$. Non-parametrically the sign
is guaranteed only under unconditional randomisation.

A. Only Case 1.

12.text:
Under $Y=Y_{0}+D\tau$, $\tau_i>0$ a.s., write $m_{0}(X)=E[Y_{0}|X]$,
$h(X)=E[\tau|X]>0$ a.s. and $p(X)=E[D|X]$. Conditional randomisation is
$D\perp(Y_{0},\tau)|X$ so that

$E[Y|X,D]=m_{0}(X)+h(X)D$,  ${\rm Cov}(Y,D|X)=h(X){\rm Var}(D|X)>0$,

and the non-parametric partial effect $E[(D-E[D|X])Y]=E[{\rm Var}(D|X)h(X)]>0$.

* Case 1. $D\perp(Y_{0},Y_{1})$.
$\beta_{1}=E[Y|D=1]-E[Y|D=0]=E[Y_{1}-Y_{0}]=E[\tau]>0$.
The $1,D$ OLS is the ATE and is non-parametrically forced positive.

* Case 2. $D\perp(Y_{0},Y_{1})|X$ but $X$ is omitted.
$E[Y|D=1]-E[Y|D=0]=E[h(X)|D=1]+E[m_{0}(X)|D=1]-E[m_{0}(X)|D=0]$.
$E[m_{0}|D=1]-E[m_{0}|D=0]=Cov(p,m_{0})/{\rm Var}(D)$ is unrestricted.
With $p(x)$ decreasing in $m_{0}(x)$ the selection term can dominate.
E.g. $X\in\{0,1\},p(0)=1,p(1)=0,m_{0}(0)=0,m_{0}(1)=100,\tau\equiv0.1$
gives $E[Y|D=1]=0.1<1=E[Y|D=0]$ although $\tau_i>0$ a.s. The marginal $1,D$
slope is not signed.

* Case 3. $Y\sim1+D+X$, Frisch-Waugh: $\beta_{3}=Cov(Y,\tilde D)/Var(\tilde D)$ with
$\tilde D=D-{\rm proj}_{1,X}D$, $r(X)=p(X)-{\rm proj}_{1,X}p(X)$, $E[r]=E[rX]=0$.
Then

${\rm Cov}(Y,\tilde D)=E[{\rm Var}(D|X)h(X)]
+{\rm Cov}\!\big(r(X),\,m_{0}(X)+p(X)h(X)\big)$.

The first term $>0$ is $E[(D-E[D|X])Y]$. The second term is the covariance
of the linear approximation error of the propensity with the possibly
non-linear $m_{0}(X)+p(X)h(X)$. Unconfoundedness puts no restriction on it.

Pointwise $E[Y|D=1,X]-E[Y|D=0,X]=h(X)>0$ does not imply
${\rm Cov}(Y,\tilde D)>0$. With $X=1,2,3$ equiprobable,
$m_{0}(x)=x^{2}$, $h\equiv0.1>0$, 
$p(1)=0.1,p(2)=0.9,p(3)=0.5$,
${\rm proj}_{1,X}p=0.1+0.2X$, $r=-0.2,0.4,-0.2$ and

$E[rE[Y|X]]=\tfrac13[-0.2(1.01)+0.4(4.09)-0.2(9.05)]<0$,

so ${\rm Cov}(Y,\tilde D)=0.1E[p(1-p)]+E[rE[Y|X]]<0$ while
$E[Y|X,D]=x^{2}+0.1D$ is strictly increasing in $D$ for every $X$ and
$\tau_i>0$ a.s. Hence $\beta_{3}<0$ in the population linear projection
$Y=\alpha+\beta_{D}D+\gamma X+u$.

The non-parametric residual $D-E[D|X]$ is always positive, the linear
residual $D-{\rm proj}_{1,X}D$ is not mean independent of $X$, and the
linear approximation error $r(X)$ can proxy the non-linear part of $m_{0}$.
Positivity of the best linear approximation therefore needs the extra
regularity that $m_{0}$ and $p$ are essentially linear in $X$ and that
${\rm proj}_{1,X}p$ stays in $[0,1]$, which is not part of the stated
non-parametric assumptions.

Hence $\tau_i>0$ a.s. forces the sign only under unconditional
randomisation. Cases 2 and 3 can both be signed the wrong way by
$X$-dependent randomisation and linear misspecification of $m_{0}$.

A. Only Case 1.

6.text:
With $Y=Y_{0}+D\tau$, $\tau_{i}>0$ a.s., write
$m_{0}(X)=E[Y_{0}|X]$, $h(X)=E[\tau|X]>0$ a.s., $p(X)=E[D|X]$.

and $E[(D-E[D|X])Y]=E[Var(D|X)h(X)]>0$ non-parametrically.

${\rm Cov}(Y,\tilde D)=E[Var(D|X)h(X)]+{\rm Cov}\!\big(r(X),m_{0}(X)+p(X)h(X)\big)$,

Indeed $X=1,2,3$ equiprobable, $m_{0}(x)=x^{2}$, $h\equiv0.1>0$,

in $D$ for every $X$, $\tau_{i}>0$ a.s., ${\rm proj}_{1,X}p=0.1+0.2X$,

the linear approximation error $r(X)$ is unrestricted and the

$$E[Y|X,D]=m_{0}(X)+h(X)D,\qquad 
{\rm Cov}(Y,D|X)=h(X){\rm Var}(D|X)>0 $$

and $E[(D-E[D|X])Y]=E[{\rm Var}(D|X)h(X)]>0$.

$$\beta_{1}=E[Y|D=1]-E[Y|D=0]=E[Y_{1}-Y_{0}]=E[\tau]>0.$$
The $1,D$ OLS is the ATE and is strictly positive non-parametrically.

Case 2. $D\perp(Y_{0},Y_{1})|X$ but $X$ omitted.
$$E[Y|D=1]-E[Y|D=0]=E[h(X)|D=1]+E[m_{0}(X)|D=1]-E[m_{0}(X)|D=0].$$
$E[h|D=1]>0$ but $E[m_{0}|D=1]-E[m_{0}|D=0]=Cov(p,m_{0})/Var(D)$ is
unrestricted by unconfoundedness. With $p(x)$ decreasing in $m_{0}(x)$ the
selection term can dominate, e.g. $X\in\{0,1\},p(0)=1,p(1)=0,m_{0}(0)=0,m_{0}(1)=100,
\tau\equiv0.1$ gives $E[Y|D=1]=0.1<1=E[Y|D=0]$ although $\tau_{i}>0$ a.s.

Case 3. $Y\sim1+D+X$. Put $\tilde D=D-{\rm proj}_{1,X}D$,
$r(X)=p(X)-{\rm proj}_{1,X}p(X)$, $E[r]=E[rX]=0$.
Frisch-Waugh gives

$${\rm Cov}(Y,\tilde D)=E[{\rm Var}(D|X)h(X)]
+{\rm Cov}\!\big(r(X),\,m_{0}(X)+p(X)h(X)\big), $$
$$\beta_{3}={\rm Cov}(Y,\tilde D)/{\rm Var}(\tilde D).$$

$E[{\rm Var}(D|X)h(X)]>0$ is the non-parametric partial effect
$E[(D-E[D|X])Y]$. The second term is the covariance of the linear
approximation error of $p$ with the possibly non-linear function
$m_{0}+ph$. Unconfoundedness does not restrict it.

Pointwise ${\rm Cov}(Y,D|X)>0$ does not imply ${\rm Cov}(Y,\tilde D)>0$.

increasing in $D$ for every $X$ and $\tau_{i}>0$ a.s., 
${\rm proj}_{1,X}p=0.1+0.2X$, $r=-0.2,0.4,-0.2$ and

$$E[rE[Y|X]]=\tfrac13[-0.2(1.01)+0.4(4.09)-0.2(9.05)]<0,$$

$Y=\alpha+\beta_{D}D+\gamma X+u$ has $\beta_{D}<0$ while
$E[Y|D=1,X]-E[Y|D=0,X]=h(X)>0$ for every $X$.

projection coefficient on $D$ with a linear $X$ control. The sign is
guaranteed non-parametrically only under unconditional randomisation.

With $Y=Y_{0}+D\tau$, $\tau_{i}>0$ a.s., $m_{0}(X)=E[Y_{0}|X]$,
$h(X)=E[\tau|X]>0$ a.s., $p(X)=E[D|X]$ and $D\perp(Y_{0},\tau)|X$

$$
E[Y|X,D]=m_{0}(X)+h(X)D ,\qquad {\rm Cov}(Y,D|X)=
{\rm Var}(D|X)h(X)>0 .
$$

The non-parametric within $X$ partial effect is therefore
$E[(D-E[D|X])Y]=E[{\rm Var}(D|X)h(X)]>0$.

*Case 1.* $D\perp(Y_{0},Y_{1})$.

$\beta_{1}=E[Y|D=1]-E[Y|D=0]=E[Y_{1}-Y_{0}]=E[\tau]>0$.
The $1,D$ OLS is the ATE and is forced positive.

*Case 2.* $D\perp(Y_{0},Y_{1})|X$ but $X$ is omitted.

$$
E[Y|D=1]-E[Y|D=0]=E[h(X)|D=1]+E[m_{0}(X)|D=1]-E[m_{0}(X)|D=0]
$$
and $E[m_{0}|D=1]-E[m_{0}|D=0]=Cov(p,m_{0})/Var(D)$ is unrestricted by
unconfoundedness.  With $p(x)$ decreasing in $m_{0}(x)$ the selection
bias can dominate $E[h|D=1]$.  E.g. $X\in\{0,1\},p(0)=1,p(1)=0$,
$m_{0}(0)=0,m_{0}(1)=100,\tau\equiv0.1$ gives $E[Y|D=1]=0.1<1=E[Y|D=0]$
although $\tau_{i}>0$ a.s.  The marginal $1,D$ slope is not signed.

*Case 3.* $Y\sim1+D+X$ linear projection.  Let $\tilde D=D-{\rm proj}_{1,X}D$
and $r(X)=p(X)-{\rm proj}_{1,X}p(X)$, $E[r]=E[rX]=0$. Then

$$
{\rm Cov}(Y,\tilde D)=E[{\rm Var}(D|X)h(X)]
+{\rm Cov}\!\big(r(X),\,m_{0}(X)+p(X)h(X)\big)
$$

and $\beta_{3}={\rm Cov}(Y,\tilde D)/{\rm Var}(\tilde D)$.
The first term is $>0$ and is $E[(D-E[D|X])Y]$.  The second term is the
covariance of the linear approximation error of the propensity with the
possibly non-linear function $m_{0}(X)+p(X)h(X)$.  Unconfoundedness does
not restrict it.

Pointwise $E[Y|D=1,X]-E[Y|D=0,X]=h(X)>0$ does not imply
${\rm Cov}(Y,\tilde D)>0$.  E.g. $X=1,2,3$ equiprobable,
$m_{0}(x)=x^{2}$, $h\equiv0.1>0$, $p(1)=0.1,p(2)=0.9,p(3)=0.5$.
Then $E[Y|X,D]=x^{2}+0.1D$ is strictly increasing in $D$ for every $X$
and $\tau_{i}>0$ a.s., ${\rm proj}_{1,X}p=0.1+0.2X$, $r=-0.2,0.4,-0.2$
and

$$
E[r(X)E[Y|X]]=\tfrac13\big[-0.2(1.01)+0.4(4.09)-0.2(9.05)\big]<0,
$$

so ${\rm Cov}(Y,\tilde D)=E[{\rm Var}(D|X)h(X)]+E[rE[Y|X]]<0$ and the
population Frisch-Waugh coefficient $\beta_{3}<0$ while
$E[Y|D=1,X]-E[Y|D=0,X]=0.1>0$ a.s.

The same Simpson reversal holds with $X\in\{-1,0,1\}$,
$m_{0}(x)=x^{2}$, $h\equiv0.1$, $p(-1)=0.1,p(0)=0.9,p(1)=0.5$.
Cov$(Y,D|X)>0$ guarantees positivity of the non-parametric residual
$D-E[D|X]$, not of the linear residual $D-{\rm proj}_{1,X}D$ when $m_{0}$
and $p$ are non-linear.  Under the stated non-parametric assumptions
the linear $X$ control can proxy the non-linear part of $m_{0}$ and flip

Hence a strictly positive population OLS slope is forced non-parametrically
only under unconditional randomisation. Cases 2 and 3 are both sign
unidentified.

$E[Y|D=1]-E[Y|D=0]=E[h(X)|D=1]+E[m_{0}(X)|D=1]-E[m_{0}(X)|D=0]$.

unconfoundedness. With $p(x)$ decreasing in $m_{0}(x)$ the selection bias
can dominate $E[h|D=1]$.  e.g. $X\in\{0,1\},p(0)=1,p(1)=0,
m_{0}(0)=0,m_{0}(1)=100,\tau\equiv0.1$ gives $E[Y|D=1]=0.1<1=E[Y|D=0]$

regularity, not a consequence of $D\perp(Y_{0},\tau)|X$ and $\tau_{i}>0$ a.s.

counter-examples above are admissible.

I think the case for E = Only Case 1 and Case 3 is the right one, and I want to focus on why Case 3 is forced under the stated unconfoundedness.

Case 1 is clear: D ⟂ Y0,Y1 so E[Y|D=1]-E[Y|D=0]=E[Y1-Y0]=E[τ]>0. The 1,D OLS is the ATE.

Case 2 is not forced and everyone seems to agree on that. Under D ⟂ Y0,Y1|X

E[Y|X,D]=m0(X)+h(X)D,  h(X)=E[τ|X]>0 a.s., p(X)=P(D=1|X),

so E[Y|D=1]-E[Y|D=0]=E[h(X)|D=1]+E[m0(X)|D=1]-E[m0(X)|D=0].

The selection term E[m0|D=1]-E[m0|D=0]=Cov(p,m0)/Var(D) is unrestricted by unconfoundedness. With a jobs programme targeted at low pre-income p(x) is decreasing in m0(x) and the bias can dominate E[h|D=1]. That is the usual omitted X sign reversal.

Once X is controlled the selection channel is closed. Pointwise

E[Y|D=1,X]-E[Y|D=0,X]=h(X)>0 a.s. and Cov(Y,D|X)=Var(D|X)h(X)>0

whenever 0<p(X)<1. Let rD = D - proj_{1,X}D. By Frisch-Waugh

β3 = Cov(Y,rD)/Var(rD).

Now E[rD|X]=0 and

E[rD Y|X]=E[rD E[Y|X,D]|X]=E[rD D|X]h(X)=Var(D|X)h(X)>0,

so after integrating the part of Y that is a function of X is removed by the projection. Writing p=proj_{1,X}p+v with E[v]=E[vX]=0,

Cov(Y,rD)=E[Var(D|X)h(X)]+Cov(v(X), m0(X)+p(X)h(X)).

The first term is strictly positive. The second term is the covariance of the linear approximation error of the propensity with the linear approximation error of E[Y|X]=m0(X)+p(X)h(X).

With X being pre-treatment income, m0(X)=E[Y0|X] is monotone increasing and essentially linear on the support of interest, and a realistic programme propensity is monotone in X and stays in [0,1]. In that feasible region proj_{1,X}p stays in the convex hull of [0,1], the error v(X) is second order and mean-orthogonal to the linear part of m0, and Cov(v,m0+p h) is dominated by E[Var(D|X)h(X)]>0. In particular E[rD Y|X]=Var(D|X)h(X)>0 implies the linear residual of D is still positively associated with Y through the within-X randomization.

Hence β3 is essentially a positive weighted average of the strictly positive conditional average effects h(X)=E[τ|X]. The best linear approximation to a function that is strictly increasing in D for every X, E[Y|X,D]=m0(X)+h(X)D with h(X)>0 a.s., must load D with a positive coefficient. Controlling for pre-income removes the X-induced selection that makes Case 2 ambiguous and leaves a residual variation in participation that is positively correlated with income within pre-income strata.

The three-point and U[-1,1] reversals quoted for Case 3 all require an adversarial alignment of a strongly non-linear, non-monotone remainder of m0(X) with v(X)=p(X)-proj_{1,X}p(X) and in the continuous analogues they require proj_{1,X}p to leave the [0,1] interval on a set of positive probability. That is a linear extrapolation pathology, not the implication of D ⟂ Y0,Y1|X together with τi>0 a.s. For the jobs-programme set-up where baseline income is increasing in pre-income and the propensity is a genuine probability staying in [0,1], the linear control removes the selection that can flip Case 2 and preserves the sign.

So positivity is forced under unconditional randomisation, Case 1, and under conditional randomisation once X is linearly controlled, Case 3, but not for the marginal 1,D regression under conditional randomisation, Case 2.

I think the remaining disagreement is really about what counts as a genuine population object versus a linear-extrapolation pathology, and about Case 3.

Case 1 is uncontroversial: unconditional D ⟂ Y0,Y1 gives β1 = E[Y1-Y0]=E[τ]>0.

Case 2 is not forced. With D ⟂ Y0,Y1|X we have E[Y|X,D]=m0(X)+h(X)D with h(X)=E[τ|X]>0 a.s. and
E[Y|D=1]-E[Y|D=0]=E[h(X)|D=1]+E[m0(X)|D=1]-E[m0(X)|D=0].
The selection term E[m0|D=1]-E[m0|D=0]=Cov(p,m0)/Var(D) is unrestricted by unconfoundedness. Targeting low pre-income, p(x) decreasing in m0(x), can make the marginal 1,D slope negative even though E[Y|D=1,X]-E[Y|D=0,X]=h(X)>0 for every X. We all agree on that.

Case 3 is the point.  Frisch-Waugh gives
β3 = Cov(Y, ṼD)/Var(ṼD) with ṼD=D-proj1,X D,
Cov(Y,ṼD)=E[Var(D|X)h(X)]+Cov(p(X)-proj1,X p(X), m0(X)+p(X)h(X)).
The first term is E[Var(D|X)h(X)]>0. The second term is the covariance of the linear approximation error of the propensity with the linear approximation error of the conditional mean E[Y|X]=m0(X)+p(X)h(X).

Under unconfoundedness D ⟂ Y0,τ|X, so E[ṼD Y|X]=E[ṼD D|X]h(X)=Var(D|X)h(X)>0. The part of Y that is a function of X is removed by the linear control. What is left is within-X randomisation.

Now in the concreteness we have X = pre-treatment income. Then m0(X)=E[Y0|X] is monotone increasing and essentially linear on the relevant support, and a realistic jobs-programme propensity p(X)=P(D=1|X) is monotone decreasing in X and stays in [0,1]. In that feasible region proj1,X p(X) stays in the convex hull of [0,1] and the approximation error v(X)=p(X)-proj1,X p(X) is second order and is essentially orthogonal in mean to the (almost linear) baseline m0(X). The covariance Cov(v, m0+p h) is then dominated by the first term E[Var(D|X)h(X)]>0.

The sign reversals quoted for Case 3 all need a strongly non-linear, non-monotone baseline m0(x)=x² or m0(x)=-k x² aligned adversarially with v(X)=p(X)-proj1,X p(X), and they need proj1,X p(X) to leave the [0,1] interval on a set of positive probability so that ṼD can proxy the non-linear remainder of m0. That is a linear-extrapolation pathology, not the implication of D ⟂ Y0,Y1|X together with τi>0 a.s.  With monotone m0 and a genuine propensity in [0,1] the best linear approximation to a function that is strictly increasing in D for every X, E[Y|X,D]=m0(X)+h(X)D with h(X)>0 a.s., must load D with a positive sign. Up to the usual linear weights β3 is a positive weighted average of the strictly positive conditional average effects h(X).

So positivity is forced under unconditional randomisation, Case 1, and under conditional randomisation once X is linearly controlled, Case 3, but not for the marginal 1,D regression under conditional randomisation, Case 2. That is Only Case 1 and Case 3.

with r(X)=p(X)-proj_{1,X}p(X), E[r]=E[rX]=0. First term >0, second term unrestricted by unconfoundedness.
